name: Stream channels (human-first group chat)
what: Open or private topic channels where people and agents post in real time; the default unit of work in a community. Channels can require a topic and cap members.
how: NIP-29 group chat kind 9 with an h tag holding the channel UUID. The channels table carries channel_type (stream/forum/dm/workflow), visibility (open/private), topic_required, max_members, topic and purpose with set_by/set_at. The relay checks membership at ingest and again at REQ time before registering a subscription.
verevonRelevance: Verevon rooms are Model Plane threads where every post triggers a model turn; a plain human-to-human stream post with agents as ordinary members is the missing baseline.
notes: Slack-like. The VISION zero-notification default per surface is documented intent; see the notification records for what code does.

name: Threads with server-computed counts and broadcast replies
what: Any message can start a thread; replies live in a panel and may optionally be sent to the channel so they also appear in the main timeline.
how: NIP-10 root/parent e-tags create a thread_metadata row per reply (root_event_id, parent_event_id, depth, reply_count, descendant_count, last_reply_at, broadcast flag). A broadcast tag of 1 marks a reply that also appears in the channel. The relay synthesizes kind 39005 thread-summary overlays at query time so clients never count replies themselves.
verevonRelevance: Verevon refuses non-owner replies into another member's thread and has no thread panel; a relay-computed thread table with depth and reply counts is the data shape to copy.
notes: Same primitives as Slack (also send to channel). Reply depth is recorded; the UI keeps human-facing threads flat and allows deeper nesting only for agent-to-agent work (base_prompt.md Threading).

name: Thread view modes: focus drawer or split pane
what: An open thread can be shown beside the channel or expanded into a larger focus drawer, and the choice is remembered.
how: ThreadViewModeToggle writes a persisted threadViewMode preference (focus or split) so the control doubles as the setting; FocusThreadDrawer and ThreadPanelSurface render the two layouts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no thread side panel; offering split and focus modes fits long agent threads that need room to breathe.
notes: Small but well-reasoned UX (the toggle shows the destination layout and a tooltip is mandatory).

name: Forum channels (async long-form lens)
what: A channel type for slow, Discourse-style discussion: a post with flat comments and up/down votes, separate from fast chat.
how: Kinds 45001 (post), 45003 (comment) and 45002 (vote); channel_type forum; ForumChannelContent and ForumComposer on desktop, a forum feature on mobile; the standalone forum composer reuses the agent-invite preparation flow. Gated behind the forum preview flag in desktop.
verevonRelevance: A second room lens (long-form, zero-notification) maps to Verevon project and case Spaces that currently cannot be created.
notes: Still preview-gated in desktop although VISION.md:21 says the desktop supports all surfaces.

name: Direct messages and group DMs (up to 9)
what: One-to-one and small group DMs that can be hidden from the sidebar per viewer and resurface automatically when new activity arrives.
how: kind 41010 opens a DM (p-tags = participants) and the relay enforces a 9-participant cap; DMs are channels with a unique participant_hash per community, so the same participant set always resolves to one DM. Kind 41012 hides; NIP-DV kind 30622 publishes the per-viewer hidden set; desktop resurfaces hidden DMs on new messages. NIP-17 gift wraps are accepted for third-party clients but not indexed.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no DMs or group DMs; participant-hash idempotent DM channels and a hide/resurface model are directly reusable.
notes: DMs are server-managed channels, not E2EE (VISION.md:100). Agents can be DM participants.

name: Edit and delete, including owner-of-agent authority
what: Authors can edit and delete their messages, and the owner of an agent can edit or delete that agent's messages; huddle start cards are immutable.
how: Edit kind 40003, deletion kind 5 (self) and 9005 (admin). canManageMessageForCurrentUser mirrors the relay rule: self-author OR the author profile carries a NIP-OA ownerPubkey equal to the viewer. Soft-deleted events remain in the audit log.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no message edit or delete; letting a human correct or retract an agent's post by ownership is a cheap, high-trust control.
notes: Edits are Buzz-only on the wire (third-party Nostr clients do not render kind 40003).

name: Reactions and quick-reaction row
what: Emoji reactions on any message with a hover quick row, picker and per-user toggle.
how: kind 7 (NIP-25) with a reactions table that tracks removed_at and the source reaction event id; the reaction channel is derived from the target event; huddles add an ephemeral kind 24810 reaction burst.
verevonRelevance: Verevon room has no reactions; a thumbs-up on an agent post is also a cheap approval and feedback signal.

name: Custom emoji palette from member-owned sets
what: Members add their own emoji and every member can use the union of everyone's sets in the community.
how: Each member signs kind 30030 emoji sets and kind 10030 emoji lists; the workspace palette is computed client-side on read (not stored state); NIP-30 emoji tags carry the image in messages; CLI emoji list/set/rm/export/import.
verevonRelevance: Low priority for Verevon, but the no-central-registry union model avoids an admin bottleneck.

name: Mentions bound to exact identities
what: Selecting a person or agent in autocomplete binds the visible name to one exact key; ambiguous typed names are rejected and namesakes get qualified labels, so a display name cannot be spoofed to redirect a mention.
how: The composer keeps a label-to-pubkey map; p tags (and a mention tag) are the recipient truth, not body text. Pasted mentions are verified asynchronously with occurrence and generation fences; sends await pending bindings. Edits can add mentions and still wake agents.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agent mentions already resolve server-side from mentioned_agent_ref, but person mentions are text-only stubs with no mention record; adopt exact-identity binding plus a server-side mention record that drives notifications.
notes: Particularly important in rooms mixing humans and many agents with similar names.

name: Rich-text composer (Tiptap) with markdown, code and spoilers
what: A WYSIWYG-plus-markdown composer with a formatting toolbar, selection formatting tray, syntax-highlighted code blocks, inline spoilers, link paste handling and emoji autocomplete.
how: Tiptap core, link and placeholder extensions with a markdown round-trip; react-markdown + remark-gfm render; shiki highlights code; spoiler marks are excluded from link-preview extraction.
verevonRelevance: Verevon reuses ChatMarkdown only; a real composer with mention and attachment support is table stakes.

name: Diff messages (kind 40008) with inline diff viewer
what: Agents and people can post a unified diff to a channel and it renders as a collapsible file diff.
how: kind 40008 message; react-diff-view based DiffViewer; CLI messages send-diff; also the trigger for the diff_posted workflow trigger.
verevonRelevance: Useful for any code-working agent in a Verevon room; render structured diffs instead of raw text.

name: Attachments and media on content-addressed storage
what: Paste, drop or attach images, video, audio and files; images become galleries, video gets a player, other files become cards.
how: Blossom (BUD-01/02) PUT /media/upload with a 50 MB limit and GET /media/{sha256}.{ext}; S3/MinIO storage with server thumbnails and blurhash; imeta tags describe each attachment; clients strip metadata and the relay rejects uploads that still carry it; media reads require auth.
verevonRelevance: Verevon room composer has no upload path; content-addressed media with metadata stripping is a good default, and room ACL must gate media reads.

name: Image markup before sending
what: Draw on an image with a pen (six colours, five widths, undo/redo) before attaching it.
how: ComposerImageEditor renders strokes in natural-image coordinates on a canvas and re-encodes the image before upload.
verevonRelevance: Nice-to-have for screenshot-driven agent feedback.

name: Voice notes and audio attachments
what: Record up to five minutes of audio and send it as an inline waveform player.
how: Audio attachments named voice-note-*, a VOICE_NOTE_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS cap, WaveMessageAttachment and AudioMessageAttachment players; mobile records with the record and just_audio packages.
verevonRelevance: Voice clips plus server-side transcription would pair with Verevon agents.

name: Frame-anchored video review comments
what: Videos open in a player with a side comment panel; comments are stamped with the playback time, can be replied to and reacted on.
how: Comments are ordinary thread replies whose content starts with a [mm:ss.mmm] timecode parsed by parseVideoReviewTimecode (regex at videoReviewTimecode.ts:7); the player optimistically merges comments and posts via onSendComment(parentEventId). Nothing new on the wire, and the text degrades gracefully in clients that ignore it.
verevonRelevance: Zero-schema anchored review comments are a cheap pattern for Verevon design or video review; the same trick works for page or line anchors.
notes: Only appears in README and code; no separate event kind.

name: Sender-side link previews
what: Pasted links show a preview card (title, site, description, image) that the sender prepared, so recipients never fetch third-party URLs.
how: The desktop Rust backend fetches the page under SSRF checks, size caps (256 KB page, 2 MB image) and per-host cooldowns, sanitizes the image, uploads it to relay media, and writes up to 8 snapshots as signed tags (title/site/description/image hash).
verevonRelevance: A privacy and zero-data-retention friendly alternative to server unfurling; relevant to Verevon ZDR propagation.
notes: Costs: previews are frozen at send time and only the desktop client authors them (INF, low confidence on mobile authoring).

name: GIF search through a relay proxy
what: A GIF picker searches KLIPY through the relay and shares the result into the message.
how: POST /gifs/search and /gifs/share on the relay with a per-minute rate limit; the API key is server-side.
verevonRelevance: Low priority; shows the proxy-with-rate-limit pattern for third-party content.

name: Drafts that survive restarts and failed sends
what: Per-channel and per-thread drafts persist locally, appear in a Drafts view in Home, and are restored with exact mention recipients if a send fails or is cancelled.
how: Local draft store with v1 to v2 migration, a revision and authoritative-empty marker so late async completions cannot resurrect cleared drafts; the mobile spec requires drafts to survive restarts and updates.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no drafts; recoverable drafts matter more when an agent invite or approval can fail mid-send.

name: Read state, unread dividers and manual mark-unread
what: Per-channel and per-thread unread with an unread divider, mark read and mark unread on any message, and cross-device sync of what you have read.
how: Two systems: NIP-RS client-encrypted kind 30078 frontier blobs plus an ov_* manual-unread override layer, and a newer relay-side private /buzz/v1 read-state API (me/sidebar, me/read-state) with eligible kinds 9, 40002, 45001 and 45003. Desktop also tracks observed-unread natively and has mark-as-read shortcuts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has room-level lastReadAt only; per-thread unread and manual unread are expected by users, and the project moved from client blobs to server-derived counts, which is the better end state.
notes: Two parallel systems that do not sync with each other (docs/buzz-v1-read-state.md); a sign of protocol-first friction. The relay serves /buzz/v1 only when BUZZ_V1_ENABLED is true, and grep found no call to it in the in-repo desktop, mobile, web or CLI code; the doc says a separate client (buzz-app) uses v1 only, so in this tree the live client path is NIP-RS plus native observed-unread.

name: Typing indicators, including agents
what: See who is typing in a channel; agents broadcast typing while working.
how: Ephemeral kind 20002 via Redis pub/sub; a ZSET keyed per channel with a 5-second window and 60-second key TTL; agents publish typing over HTTP POST /events; BUZZ_ACP_NO_TYPING disables it for a harness.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has typing in presence rows (8 s decay); extend it to agents as first-class typers.

name: Presence, auto-away and status with expiry
what: Online, away and offline dots; auto-away from OS idle time; manual away or appear-offline; custom status text and emoji that expires.
how: Presence is a TTL lease: a kind 20001 heartbeat sets a Redis key with a 180-second expiry (3x a 60-second heartbeat). Desktop reads OS idle seconds to compute automatic status and stores a presence preference (auto, away, offline). Status is NIP-38 kind 30315 with expiration. For agents, availability means conversational presence, not process health.
verevonRelevance: Verevon presence is a 30 s TTL with online/typing/offline only; adding OS-idle auto-away and expiring status is straightforward.
notes: ARCHITECTURE.md:296 calls multi-node presence future work, but handlers/event.rs:989 publishes presence to the community global Redis topic, so the doc is stale.

name: Deep links and entity link chips
what: buzz:// links open messages, channels, repos, PRs, issues and projects; pasted links render as rich chips or cards, like GitHub links.
how: Scheme handler in the Tauri shell (deep_link.rs) with an allowlisted ENTITY_LINK_HOSTS set; BuzzLinkChip and MessageLinkPill render them; CLI commands return a link field that agents are told to paste verbatim so the desktop renders previews.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs stable, shareable room, message and run links with rich chips; the agent-returns-a-link convention is useful.

name: System messages and membership notices
what: Channel state changes (joins, leaves, renames) and membership notifications show as system rows; relay-signed notices tell a user they were added to or removed from a channel.
how: kind 40099 system message; kinds 44100/44101 stored community-globally with p and h tags, signed only by the relay keypair so clients cannot forge them.
verevonRelevance: Needed for Verevon member and agent add/remove events to appear in the room timeline.

name: [Not built] Scheduled send
what: No way to schedule a message from any client although a kind is reserved.
how: kind 40006 is defined and accepted by relay ingest, but no desktop, mobile or CLI path produces it.
verevonRelevance: Absent in Verevon too; low priority.
notes: Absence established by grep across desktop/src, mobile/lib and crates/buzz-cli (confidence medium).

name: [Not built] Message pins, saved items, polls and forwarding
what: None of these has user-facing UI; pin and bookmark kinds exist only as registry entries and polls are listed as planned culture features.
how: kinds 40004 (pinned), 40005 (bookmarked), 10001 (pin list) and 10003 (bookmark list) are defined; VISION.md:181 lists native polls as planned; no forwarding code found.
verevonRelevance: Verevon lacks these as well; pins and saved items are cheap wins once messages are first-class records.
notes: Grep of desktop/src for pinned found only layout pinning; NIP-ER notes a reminder without a due time can act as a bookmark but the UI always asks for a time.

name: Community = tenant boundary selected by URL, with a multi-community client
what: A workspace is reached by its URL; one client can hold many communities side by side (rail on desktop, animated switcher on mobile) with cross-community unread, and a hosted operator can serve many communities on shared infrastructure.
how: Every connection binds req.community = resolve_host(host) before AUTH, EVENT, REQ, REST, media, git, search, workflow or pub/sub handling; unknown hosts fail closed; community_id leads every primary key. Desktop keeps a community list with drag-sorted CommunityRail, per-community unread observers and per-community theme; hosted community limit raised to fifty in v0.5.28.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Spaces live inside an org and the browser has no multi-org switcher; the host-derived tenant fence and per-community unread are worth copying for users who belong to several orgs.
notes: The isolation story is backed by TLA+ and Tamarin models plus a conformance replay crate (see governance records).

name: Roles and permissions: community owner/admin/member, channel owner/admin/member/guest/bot
what: Community owners and admins moderate and manage membership; each channel has its own owner/admin/member/guest/bot roles with a strict hierarchy and last-owner protection.
how: MemberRole hierarchy Owner > Admin > Member > Guest; pure policy functions in channel_authz.rs decide role grants, role changes, self-departure and the sole-owner rule; elevated grants require an elevated actor; roles are a closed enum, not capability sets.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has fixed viewer/editor/manager/owner roles and no role editor; Buzz shows role change flows and last-owner guards, but its own roles are coarse (no per-capability grants).
notes: Moderation is explicitly built as capabilities so a moderator tier is a policy change (VISION_MODERATION.md:61).

name: Relay-level membership (NIP-43), operator roles and allowlist
what: Operators decide who may join the relay at all: add, remove and re-role members, publish a membership list, optionally restrict to an allowlist, and set the workspace icon.
how: Admin command kinds 9030-9033, relay-signed kind 13534 membership list, buzz-admin CLI (add-member, remove-member, list-members, generate-key, deletions), optional pubkey_allowlist table, NIP-OA delegation fallback so an owner's agent is admitted with its owner.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Verevon org-level membership; the agent-admitted-via-owner fallback is the pattern for personal agents needing no separate seat.

name: Channel visibility, directory and self-join
what: Open channels are searchable and self-joinable; private channels are hidden and invite-only; a channel browser lists joinable channels with a pinned create row.
how: Open/private visibility on the channel row; open-channel directory fetched separately from the 60-second membership poll so the poll stays bounded; kind 9021 join request adds a member and emits system and discovery events; ChannelBrowserDialog keeps keyboard order identical to visual order.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no room discovery or self-join; an open/private split with a directory is the Slack baseline.

name: Agent add policy (owner_only, nobody, anyone)
what: Each agent declares who may add it to channels, so a stranger cannot draft your personal agent into their room.
how: Per-agent channel_add_policy enforced inside kind 9000 handling: owner_only requires the actor to be the agent's owner, nobody blocks third-party adds, anyone allows them; self-add bypasses agent policy but not private-channel auth; CLI channels setaddpolicy.
verevonRelevance: Directly relevant to Verevon personal agents: a personal agent needs an add-policy so other rooms cannot pull it in without its owner.

name: Channel lifecycle: archive, TTL ephemeral channels, topic and purpose
what: Channels can be archived, unarchived, deleted or created with a time-to-live; topic and purpose are editable by any member while name and description are admin-only.
how: channels.ttl_seconds and ttl_deadline with an expiry index; huddle backing channels are created with a one-hour TTL and hidden from lists; kind 9002 edit-metadata splits permissions (name/about admin, topic/purpose any member); EphemeralChannelBadge marks TTL channels.
verevonRelevance: Ephemeral TTL rooms fit short-lived Verevon work Spaces (incident or run rooms) that archive themselves.

name: Stateless invite codes and join policy acceptance
what: Owners and admins mint invite codes with a TTL and max-uses; invitees claim them (even before being members) after accepting the community terms and privacy policy; a web landing page and deep link carry the code.
how: POST /api/invites (NIP-98, owner/admin) and POST /api/invites/claim (exempt from membership gate; HMAC on the code proves admin authorization); default TTL 72 h; claim rate limit 10 per minute per pubkey; join-policy acceptances stored per community; web route invite/$code and desktop useClaimInvite.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has org invites at org level but nothing for room-scoped or guest invites; a stateless HMAC token avoids an invite table.

name: Guest role (label with weak enforcement)
what: A guest role exists and can be chosen when adding members or agents, but its restrictions are thin.
how: MemberRole::Guest is rank 1 in the hierarchy; the only enforced difference found is that guests and bots cannot push to protected git refs; VISION.md describes scoped guest tokens for investors and reporters that were not found in code.
verevonRelevance: External or guest collaboration is a gap in both products; Verevon should design guest scope (per-room, read-only, expiring) rather than copy Buzz's label.
notes: Medium confidence: absence of read-only message enforcement is based on grep, not a full authz audit. A scoped API-token store (scopes plus a per-channel allowlist, expiry and revocation) exists in schema and buzz-db, but no relay or auth path authenticates with it, so the guest-token idea in VISION.md has no live implementation.

name: [Not built] Teams, user groups, @here/@channel and shared channels
what: There is no org-level team or group concept, no @channel or @here broadcast mention, and no channel shared across communities.
how: The kind registry reserves a user-groups range (47000-47999) with no kinds defined; grep for here/channel/everyone mentions and user groups found none; communities are strictly isolated.
verevonRelevance: Teams-style team/channel hierarchy and guest-shared channels remain unsolved in both Buzz and Verevon; do not expect inspiration here.
notes: Buzz uses the word team only for groups of agent personas (kind 30176).

name: Channel templates bundling a canvas and an agent roster
what: Create a channel from a template that carries the description, type, visibility, a starter canvas and a roster of personas or teams to add with a runtime, model, role and backend.
how: ChannelTemplateRecord with canvas_template and TemplateAgentRoster (personas and teams with runtime, model, role and Local/Provider backend); create, list, update, duplicate, delete commands; useApplyTemplate. Stored per desktop in channel-templates.json, not on the relay.
verevonRelevance: A Space template (instructions plus bound agents plus starter doc) is a natural Verevon feature, but store it server-side per org; Buzz keeps it local so teammates cannot share it.
notes: Local storage is the key weakness.

name: Starter channels and an agent-led welcome kickoff
what: New communities get #general and #welcome-everyone, and a built-in agent (Fizz) opens a welcome thread, teammates introduce themselves in-thread, and Fizz closes it.
how: ensure_starter_channels creates deterministic-UUID open channels and joins them; welcomeKickoff choreography with opener, thread intros and closer; failedAfterKickoff reads real agent state; the failure-path doc concludes facts must decide, timers are only a backstop.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's empty room needs an onboarding story; an agent greeter works, but copy the post-mortem lessons (no timer-driven permanent claims, no runaway agent chatter).
notes: Two of three failure classes listed as still open in the doc.

name: Keypair identity, key backup, device pairing and identity archive
what: Identity is a secp256k1 key held by the client; onboarding walks through download and encrypted backup, a second device can be paired by QR or typed code with a short authentication string, and old identities can be archived.
how: NIP-49 ncryptsec and HPKE-wrapped key backups, an egress guard that blocks key-backup material from reaching the relay, NIP-AB ephemeral pairing over a sidecar pair relay (kind 24134) with SAS confirmation, identity recovery pairing, NIP-IA archive and unarchive requests.
verevonRelevance: Verevon uses account auth, so raw key custody is not needed; copy only the phone-pairing UX (QR plus short code) for connecting a mobile client.
notes: Key custody is a real onboarding hazard; no NIP-AB spec file exists, the spec lives in code (scout finding verified).

name: Admin consoles (platform staff and operators)
what: Desktop has an Admin Console for platform staff (reports, feedback, communities, direct actions, staffing) and a small admin web SPA lists open reports and product feedback.
how: Desktop admin-console feature with about 25 admin_* commands and a Staffing tab; admin-web is a 1,000-line SPA reading /reports and /feedback with NIP-98; staff can ban, timeout and delete directly with a staff guard.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs a Space-scoped admin view (members, agents, policies); Buzz's consoles target platform operators, not tenant admins, so they are only partial inspiration.
notes: Tenant admin tasks (members, roles, channel settings) live in the regular desktop UI.

name: Member roster and agent controls in the channel
what: A members sidebar and management sheet list people and agents with roles, presence, add/remove, role change, kick and per-agent controls (start, stop, respond-to).
how: MembersSidebar, MembersSidebarAgentControls, ChannelManagementSheet and AddChannelBot dialogs; relay GET /members/search for people search; roster freshness rules and admin-kick tests.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon Members tab is read-only plus add/remove; combining humans and agents in one roster with inline controls is the better layout.

name: Workspace profile and per-community theme
what: Admins set a workspace icon every client sees; each community can carry its own theme.
how: NIP-WP kind 9033 writes the icon into the NIP-11 relay information document; community theme stored as a kind 30078 event and applied by CommunityThemeController.
verevonRelevance: Org branding in Verevon Spaces is a cosmetic extra.

name: Mentioning a non-member asks for consent to invite them (with a safe default)
what: If you @mention someone who is not in the channel, a dialog offers to invite them, to send without inviting, or to cancel; in a private channel you cannot administer, inviting is withheld and the reason is explained.
how: NonMemberMentionDialog takes canInvite, a pending state and an error; the safe action receives focus; publication can require invitation of the intended recipients; the draft is restored on cancel or failure; admission rules come from channelMemberAdmission.
verevonRelevance: Verevon @agent mentions resolve only against bound agents; a consent step for mentioning someone outside the Space avoids both silent no-ops and accidental disclosure.
notes: Same flow powers the agent mention-to-invite path (see agents records).

name: Human-readable handles per community (NIP-05) for people and agents
what: People and agents can carry a name@community handle that other clients can verify; the same key can have a different handle in each community.
how: A public GET /.well-known/nostr.json binds the request host to its community before a tenant-scoped lookup; users.nip05_handle is unique per community on lower-case; profiles are per-community kind 0 events reposted on joining.
verevonRelevance: A stable, verifiable handle for each agent and person is useful for audit labels and mentions in Verevon; derive it from Control subject ids rather than a separate directory.
notes: Cheap but only meaningful inside the community that issued it.

name: Channel huddles over a relay-hosted Opus audio room
what: Any channel can start a voice huddle; members join with their microphone, mute, react and leave; the huddle appears as a card in the parent channel and ends when the last person leaves.
how: WebSocket /huddle/{channel}/audio on the relay with NIP-42 auth and a membership check, an in-memory room forwarding opaque Opus frames with an 8-byte header (sequence, 48 kHz timestamp, dBov level, flags), MAX_PEERS_PER_ROOM 25, bounded drop-on-full audio channels and a never-dropping control channel. A hidden 1-hour TTL backing channel hosts the huddle chat; kinds 48100-48106 record lifecycle.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no calls; Buzz proves a no-SFU small-room voice path that reuses channel membership as the only gate and lets agents be peers.
notes: Voice only (no video or screen share); a 25-peer soft cap, 255 hard cap.

name: Desktop voice engine: jitter buffer, push-to-talk and reconnect
what: Huddle audio on desktop has adaptive playout, push-to-talk with a global shortcut, a companion window and automatic reconnection.
how: Opus codec with NetEq jitter buffer (jitter.rs), rodio output, rubato resampling, earshot VAD, global Ctrl+Space push-to-talk (ptt_shortcut.rs), window-level Ctrl+Shift+Space huddle toggle, reconnect.rs, companion huddle window and an audio-device picker.
verevonRelevance: Only relevant if Verevon adds calls; the NetEq plus Opus choice is a solid reference stack.
notes: About 15,800 lines of Rust in the huddle module (wc across src-tauri/src/huddle).

name: Voice agents in huddles with local speech, floor control and barge-in
what: Agents can be added to a huddle, listen to humans through on-device speech-to-text, speak back with per-agent synthetic voices, and stop talking when a human starts.
how: Local STT with sherpa-onnx and earshot VAD (300 ms silence flush) feeds transcripts to agents; local Pocket TTS synthesizes 24 kHz audio published through a socket authenticated as the agent so roster attribution stays correct; HumanFloor and LocalBargeIn coordinate cancellation (20 consecutive VAD frames on coupled output); per-agent voice registry and import.
verevonRelevance: Verevon only has Model Gateway AI realtime voice outside rooms; agent-as-attributed-audio-peer with a human-floor policy is the design to follow if rooms get voice.
notes: Voice work runs on the hosting human's machine, so agent speech depends on that desktop being present.

name: Huddle transcript posted into the huddle chat
what: Optionally transcribe a huddle; segments appear as chat messages in the huddle's companion chat, where people and agents can also type.
how: set_huddle_transcription_enabled starts or tears down the STT pipeline and invalidates in-flight transcript tasks; transcript segments are posted as messages to the ephemeral huddle channel; HuddleTranscriptIntro explains the combined chat.
verevonRelevance: A transcript-as-messages approach gives Verevon meeting notes the same search and agent-context path as chat.
notes: No caption overlay, no recap or summary, and no recording (ARCHITECTURE.md:942 limitation 4).

name: Mobile huddle (foreground-only MVP)
what: Mobile users can start or join a huddle with the microphone, hear several participants, mute and leave; a relaunch rebuilds the visible card without silently reopening the mic.
how: Separate WebSocket to /huddle/{id}/audio with challenge, NIP-42 signed kind 22242 and protocol_version 2, explicit joined handshake, bounded reconnect backoff (0, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000 ms), a fetch of the kind 39002 snapshot to decide whether the last human leaving ends the huddle.
verevonRelevance: Reference for conservative failure handling (a failed member count assumes someone is still present).

name: [Not built] Video, screen share, recording, AI recap, calendar, whiteboard
what: Huddles are audio only: no camera, no screen share, no recording or recap, no meeting scheduling.
how: Recording and per-track publishing are reserved kinds without a producer; grep found no screen-share, whiteboard or calendar code.
verevonRelevance: Both Buzz and Verevon lack the Teams meeting stack; Buzz adds nothing to copy beyond voice and local transcription.

name: Tenant-scoped full-text search with per-hit re-authorization
what: Search across messages the caller may see, ordered by relevance, with prefix typeahead for the top bar.
how: Postgres generated tsvector search_tsv (simple config, GIN index) on the events table; encrypted and private routing kinds are excluded at the storage level; SearchQuery requires a community id; the relay refetches every candidate through a community-scoped fetcher and applies the access predicate per hit, so search is never the access boundary; SearchMode::Prefix serves typeahead.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no message search; the rule that search returns candidates and the owner plane re-authorizes each hit fits the no-cross-plane-DB constraint.
notes: The simple tsvector config has no stemming or stop words; the project migrated from a Typesense sidecar to Postgres FTS (comment in events.sql).

name: Slack-style search operators and scoped search
what: Type from:, in:, after: and before: in the search box; Ctrl/Cmd+K searches everything and Ctrl/Cmd+F searches the current channel with a removable scope chip.
how: parseSearchOperators splits operators at token boundaries (invalid dates stay in the text), resolves names at the call site, converts dates to NIP-01 since/until semantics (Slack-compatible exclusive before); SearchDialogInputRow shows the scope chip; useHistorySearchState keeps history.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the same operator grammar for room search; the bound-at-token-start rule is a useful detail.
notes: Multi-word handles are a known limitation (comment in parseSearchOperators).

name: People and channel discovery
what: Find people and agents by name when mentioning or starting a DM, and browse joinable channels.
how: GET /members/search and search_users, mention candidate ranking (mentionRanking.ts), open channel directory, New Message screen with recipient results.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has a per-Space roster and org members list but no cross-org or cross-Space directory.

name: History as agent memory: agents search the log with the CLI
what: The pitch is that an agent can answer 'have we seen this error before?' by searching months of channel history and posting the threads.
how: Agents call buzz messages search/get/thread through the agent CLI against the same FTS index; there is no separate retrieval store.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Verevon grounded room turns, which use Data Plane retrieval instead of raw chat search.
notes: Marketing claim tied to plain FTS; no ranking over patches, runs and approvals beyond what shares the events table.

name: [Not built] Semantic search, AI answers and cross-source search
what: No embeddings, no AI-generated search answers, no file directory beyond media references.
how: No vector or embedding dependency found in buzz-search, buzz-db or migrations; search covers the events table only.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can differentiate with Data Plane v2 semantic retrieval inside rooms; Buzz has none.

name: Home inbox with eight filters and inline reply
what: Home is a personal list-plus-detail inbox of what needs you: filters for All, Projects, Mentions, Threads, Needs action, Agents, Reminders and Drafts, with context messages and an inline reply composer in the detail pane.
how: Relay feed queries assemble mentions (event_mentions join on a community-leading index), needs_action (workflow approval requests and stream reminders addressed to you), activity and agent_activity, fan-out-on-read, capped at 100 rows; the desktop groups items by conversation root and keeps per-conversation selection, draft and local-reply state.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Space Activity is room-scoped; a personal cross-room inbox with a Needs-action lane (approvals, reminders, agent asks) is the attention surface Verevon lacks.
notes: Email-like layout; Agents filter groups agent notes and job events.

name: Per-event notification slots, sounds and thread-aware rules
what: Choose which events alert you (DMs, mentions, thread replies, needs action, agent job events), pick a sound per slot, toggle the home badge, and decide whether to alert while viewing the channel.
how: NotificationSettings v2 with per-slot alert flags and sound names; shouldNotifyForEvent lets a mention through always, then applies channel mutes, then thread rules (participated, followed, authored roots, muted roots); native notifications via tauri-plugin-notification with a Windows shim fix.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no Space-originated notifications; the slot model (event type x sound x enable) and thread-participation rule are a ready template.

name: Follow and mute threads and channels
what: Follow any thread (even before the first reply), unfollow, mute a thread or a channel; muting and sidebar organization sync across devices.
how: Follow/unfollow in MessageActionBar; thread activity persistence tracks participated and authored roots; per-user mutes, stars, sections and sort stored as kind 30078 events with a last-writer-wins map and sync watermarks.
verevonRelevance: Needed for Verevon rooms with many agent threads; syncing per-user prefs as relay-stored replaceable state is simple and multi-device-safe.

name: Reminders and snooze (encrypted, relay-scheduled)
what: Remind me later on any message with presets (30 min, 1 h, 3 h, tomorrow 9am, next Monday); due reminders alert, appear under Needs action and a Reminders panel.
how: NIP-ER kind 30300: target, note and status are NIP-44 encrypted to the author; only a public not_before tag tells supporting relays when to emit a due signal; clients enforce not_before locally; reminderNotificationPoll drives alerts.
verevonRelevance: Cheap, high-value attention tool Verevon lacks; encrypting the target while exposing only the due time is a nice privacy detail.
notes: Recurrence is intentionally out of scope.

name: Mobile push as a content-free wake (APNs), enrolled with App Attest
what: iOS devices get a wake-up push; the app extension then fetches and signature-verifies the real message from the relay and renders a rich notification locally, so no content passes through Apple.
how: NIP-PL kind 30350 push leases (encrypted, installation-scoped, expiring) matched by the relay with read-authorization checks and a durable wake queue; a standalone buzz-push-gateway holds the APNs credentials, validates Apple App Attest and issues opaque capabilities; relay advertises buzz-push-v1; iOS NotificationService extension resolves content. Android push is not implemented.
verevonRelevance: Verevon notification-core has Novu delivery disabled by default and ZDR not proven; a content-free wake plus client-side fetch is the ZDR-compatible mobile push design.
notes: Marked experimental in docs/buzz-push.md; README lists push under strong opinions pending code, so docs lag the code; APNs only (no FCM or UnifiedPush found).

name: Mobile push suppression while the desktop is active (draft spec)
what: When you are active on a desktop connected to the community, the relay withholds mobile pushes for ten minutes after your last activity.
how: Draft rules: desktop sends renewable suppression signals every 10 s (30 s stale expiry, 5 s tolerance), relay enforces and the gateway stays agnostic, signals are separate from visible presence and never broadcast, suppressed pushes are discarded not replayed.
verevonRelevance: Verevon cross-device alerting will need the same desktop-first suppression to avoid double alerts; the privacy rules (no activity history, uncertain means send anyway) are reusable.
notes: Status line says draft, not ready for implementation.

name: System tray menu showing running and recent agent activity
what: The tray lists agents currently running or recently active and offers quick actions while the window is hidden.
how: The webview projects agent-turn state into a small native menu (Running and Recent sections, take/requeue tray actions); macOS prevent-sleep keeps agents alive while turns run.
verevonRelevance: Relevant only if Verevon ships a desktop shell; the idea of agent activity outside the window generalizes to notifications.

name: Unread badges, overflow button and cross-community unread
what: Sidebar shows unread dots and counts, a More-unread button when unread channels are off-screen, a home badge, and unread state for other communities in the rail.
how: Observed-unread persistence in native code, useSidebarUnreadOverflow, home badge subtotal rules and a community unread observer.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has room-level unread only for the open room and no cross-room aggregate; copy the overflow and rail aggregate patterns.

name: Agent job notification slots (wired but dead)
what: Settings expose sounds for agent job accepted, progress, result and error, but nothing emits those events.
how: SOUND_SLOTS include job_* slots; the code comment states the job protocol kinds 43001-43006 are defined and queryable but buzz-acp publishes plain stream messages, so the rows render disabled.
verevonRelevance: Lesson for Verevon: a typed agent-job event family was designed but agents coordinate through ordinary chat; keep run status as a first-class server record (Verevon runs) rather than inventing parallel message kinds.
notes: Doc and code agree here; the scout listed the job kinds as live multi-agent coordination, which they are not.

name: Zero-notification defaults per surface (documented intent)
what: The vision says streams and forums notify nobody by default, DMs notify only urgent items, workflows notify only approvals, and you opt in to noise.
how: Documented as a design rule in the Surfaces and Home Feed sections; desktop code instead notifies for mentions, DMs and thread rules by default, so the zero default is not enforced as a relay setting.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should decide attention defaults explicitly (agent-heavy rooms are noisy); an opt-in-to-noise default is a defensible stance.
notes: Treat as vision, not behaviour.

name: [Not built] Do not disturb, quiet hours and digests
what: No DND schedule, quiet hours, email digest or notification summary.
how: Suppression spec rule 6 defers a future DND; grep found no DND, digest or email-notification code.
verevonRelevance: Verevon plans quiet hours under S4.4; Buzz offers no reference beyond the suppression idea.

name: Pulse: a social notes feed with people, liked and agent tabs (preview)
what: A separate feed shows short public notes from people and agents, with Everyone, People, Liked, Agents and Mine tabs, search, likes and a composer; consecutive notes from one agent within five minutes collapse into a single activity card with a status dot.
how: Kind 1 notes and kind 7 reactions queried through get_global_notes, get_user_notes and get_notes_timeline and published with publish_note; contact lists (kind 3) drive the People tab; groupAgentNotes folds runs of agent notes by pubkey and time window; the surface is preview-gated.
verevonRelevance: A feed where agents post digestible updates for the whole workspace is an alternative to noisy room posts; collapsing bursts by agent and time window is a cheap noise reducer for Verevon Activity.
notes: Public-style social feed inside a work tool; value unproven (still behind a preview flag).

name: YAML-as-code workflow engine with traces
what: Channel-scoped automations fire on a message, a reaction, a posted diff, a cron or interval schedule, or an inbound webhook and run ordered steps with conditions, templating and delays, leaving a trace of every step.
how: buzz-workflow parses YAML with serde (triggers are internally tagged by on:, actions by action:), evaluates if-conditions with evalexpr (custom string functions, 100 ms timeout), resolves single-pass templates, runs under a 100-permit semaphore, a 60-second cron loop; execution kinds 46001-46012 are excluded from re-triggering. Actions: send_message (with reply_in_thread), add_reaction, call_webhook, delay work; send_dm and set_channel_topic return NotImplemented.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has agent schedules but no event-triggered automation inside rooms; a trigger-condition-action layer with run traces would complement agents.
notes: ARCHITECTURE.md lists four triggers; code has five (diff_posted). The stub status of two actions is verified as current.

name: Workflow authoring UI (form builder, cron input, run trace)
what: Build workflows in a form with a cron helper, a no-code message-text condition editor, a webhook secret dialog and a step-by-step run trace, or edit YAML.
how: features/workflows/ui with WorkflowFormBuilder, CronExpressionInput, WorkflowMessageTextConditionEditor, WorkflowRunTrace, WorkflowApprovalCard; conditions compile to evalexpr strings; preview-gated.
verevonRelevance: Only worth borrowing the trace view; Verevon runs already have richer run records.

name: Workflow approval gates (UI and API exist, executor fails the run)
what: A request_approval step is meant to pause a workflow until someone grants or denies; today a run that reaches one is marked failed.
how: Schema, REST endpoints under /workflows/{id}/runs/{run}/approvals, grant and deny kinds 46030/46031, approval cards and needs-action feed items exist; the executor returns Suspended with a token but finalize_run records code approval_not_supported because the token and resume are not persisted (WF-08).
verevonRelevance: Same failure mode as Verevon (granted approval does not resume the paused run): persist the continuation first, then build UI; do not ship approval cards that cannot resume work.
notes: Verified against code; unchanged since the architecture doc.

name: Inbound and outbound webhooks with SSRF protection
what: Any workflow can expose a secret webhook URL, and workflows can call external URLs.
how: POST /hooks/{id} authenticated by a constant-time comparison of a stored secret (not an HMAC of the body); call_webhook uses an SSRF deny list, redirects disabled and a 1 MiB response cap; git hook secrets use HMAC.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has legacy webhooks not tied to Spaces; the enumerated-deny SSRF helper is reusable.

name: Signed-event HTTP bridge for non-WebSocket clients
what: Agents and scripts can read and write through plain HTTP with signed requests instead of holding a WebSocket.
how: POST /events, /query and /count with NIP-98 per-request auth and replay guards; extension fields such as before_id, depth_limit, feed_types and channel-window flags; same ingest pipeline as WebSocket EVENT.
verevonRelevance: The Verevon BFF plays this role; per-request signature plus replay guard is a simple agent-auth option.

name: Agent-first CLI as the primary agent surface
what: Every platform action (messages, channels, DMs, reactions, canvas, workflows, repos, PRs, issues, memory, moderation) is available from one JSON-in JSON-out CLI that agents drive from a shell.
how: buzz-cli has about 25 command groups, structured JSON stdout, typed exit codes (0 ok, 1 user, 2 network, 3 auth, 4 other, 5 write conflict), two-tier auth, a help tree agents read once, and base_prompt.md teaches the CLI instead of per-tool schemas. Agents also receive deep-link fields to paste into messages.
verevonRelevance: Verevon exposes 14 spaces.* action IDs with a drift guard; offering the same registry as a CLI inside the agent sandbox is an alternative to tool schemas and keeps one source of truth.
notes: Shell-driven control means tool calls are opaque shell strings; the desktop parses them back into semantic cards (see activity render classes).

name: MCP tool server and lifecycle hooks with injection-safe output
what: Agents get a small MCP server (shell, read_file, view_image, str_replace, todo) and can attach more MCP servers; underscore-prefixed hook tools run at defined points and cannot be called by the model.
how: buzz-dev-mcp runs ephemeral process groups with bounded output; hooks _Stop (objection keeps the agent going) and _PostCompact are filtered from the model's tool list and rejected if called directly; hook output is JSON-encoded and injected as tool results of lower trust; per-agent MCP server editor in desktop.
verevonRelevance: The hook convention (todo-enforcement on stop, context-restore after compaction) is a lightweight way to add policy to Verevon agent loops.

name: Bring-your-own agent runtime through ACP (14 known harnesses plus custom)
what: Choose which agent runtime powers each agent: goose, Claude Code, Codex, the built-in buzz-agent, Cursor, Devin, Hermes, OpenClaw, Kimi, Amp, Grok and more, or define a custom ACP command; the app probes installs and logins and shows readiness.
how: A single Rust catalog (KnownAcpRuntime) declares commands, env keys, install and auth probes and capabilities per harness and is projected to the UI; custom harness JSON; effort, model and provider fields rendered from descriptors; skills are symlinked per harness skill directory.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agents run only on Model Plane runtimes; admitting external ACP agents (Codex, Cursor, Hermes) as room members would make Spaces a neutral room, at the cost of weaker sandbox guarantees.
notes: Runtime facts are deliberately single-sourced in Rust; a rule worth copying.

name: Persona packs and snapshots as portable agent definitions
what: Agent personas and teams can be packaged (plugin manifest plus persona markdown plus skills) and validated with the CLI, and running agents can be exported as snapshots to import elsewhere.
how: buzz-persona parses .plugin/plugin.json and *.persona.md with frontmatter triggers and hooks; buzz pack validate and inspect; desktop imports snapshots (.agent.json, .team.json), not pack source; example pack meadow-core has an orchestrator and two reviewers.
verevonRelevance: A portable, versioned definition of an agent team is useful for Verevon marketplace and templates, but Buzz itself admits pack runtime integration is not implemented.
notes: Corrects the scout: persona packs are a spec plus CLI, not a working desktop import path.

name: Slash commands are agent pass-through only
what: Agent-defined slash commands are forwarded to the agent as text; there is no platform command registry or composer command menu.
how: buzz-acp records available_commands_update from ACP agents and passes slash text through; AcpCommandField discovers commands only to configure agents.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has a / skill picker in the room composer, which is ahead of Buzz here.

name: Feature flags and preview gating
what: Unfinished areas (workflows, projects, pulse, forum, agent-managed profiles) are behind opt-in experimental toggles, and an internal-only overlay exposes extra features such as Bestie.
how: preview-features.json drives an ExperimentalFeaturesCard; typed boolean and integer flags with a LaunchDarkly evaluator in buzz-feature-flags; protectedFeatures/internal.ts defines internal-only features that the OSS build exports as an empty list.
verevonRelevance: A small preview-toggle registry would let Verevon ship Space features to testers without per-org policy rows.

name: Rust SDK and example bot
what: Typed event builders, a WebSocket client and a runnable NIP-42 example bot show how to build non-agent bots.
how: buzz-sdk builders, buzz-ws-client, buzz-test-client and examples/countdown-bot with deterministic commands.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has an action registry and AG-UI stream rather than an external SDK; no direct lesson.

name: In-app product feedback form
what: Users can send feedback (with attachments) from settings and operators read it in the admin SPA.
how: kind 42000 product feedback stored per community with attachments; /feedback routes served to platform staff; SendFeedbackDialog in desktop.
verevonRelevance: Cheap feedback loop Verevon could embed in rooms.

name: [Not built] App directory, marketplace, tabs, form builder and OpenAPI
what: No app store, no pinned apps or tabs inside channels, no general form builder and no OpenAPI spec for Buzz's own API.
how: Grep found no marketplace or tab-surface code; openapi appears only inside Kubernetes client types.
verevonRelevance: Both products lack the Slack and Teams app ecosystem; Verevon planned S5.4 governed app build and publish is a differentiator opportunity.

name: Scoped API tokens exist in the store but are not authenticated by the relay
what: A table and data layer for named API tokens with scopes, an optional channel allowlist, expiry and revocation is present, but the relay authenticates with keypair signatures instead.
how: api_tokens rows hold a 32-byte token hash, owner, scopes (messages, channels, users, jobs, files, repos and admin variants) and channel_ids; create, list and revoke functions exist in buzz-db; no route, handler or auth path reads them (grep of buzz-relay and buzz-auth found none); BUZZ_API_TOKEN is still a reserved agent environment key.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can skip this; it shows that the third-party-app path (scoped tokens) was abandoned in favor of per-request signatures, leaving no easy way to issue a limited credential to an external integration.
notes: Dormant or legacy code; confidence medium because of grep-level reasoning.

name: Agents are keypair members with a bot role, attested owner and visible provenance
what: Every agent has its own key, profile and channel membership like a person, is marked as an agent, and is shown as managed by its owner; the same affordances and audit trail apply to people and agents.
how: secp256k1 identity per agent; NIP-OA auth tag (owner signs agent pubkey plus conditions) travels on the agent's events and in its kind 0 profile; kind 10100 agent profile carries runtime status; MemberRole::Bot; BotIdenticon and MessageAgentOwner label messages; a cloud marker says Not managed on this device when no local record exists.
verevonRelevance: Verevon models agents as Control service subjects plus Convex bindings; adding a visible managed-by attribution on every agent post and an attested ownership chain would make accountability legible in the room.
notes: Mobile relabelled owned by to managed by (mobile CHANGELOG 0.4.7).

name: Delegated authority: an agent inherits access through its owner attestation
what: An agent can be admitted to a closed relay, or push to a protected branch, because its owner is admitted or listed, without a separate seat.
how: Relay membership falls back to the NIP-OA owner when the agent itself is not a member; git push policy gives an agent managed by the repository owner the owner role on that repo (is_agent_owner lookup), while the VISION_PROJECTS form where any listed maintainer carries their agents is designed, not implemented; removing the owner from a closed relay stops the admission fallback for all their agents; unattested agents must be admitted explicitly.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Verevon owner-plane ACL rules: agent authority derives from an accountable owner and dies with the owner's access, which is the safe default for personal agents.
notes: The same property creates the confused-deputy risk the information-flow draft addresses.

name: Personal agents run under the owner desktop as supervised local processes
what: Users create agents from personas, then start, stop and restart them from the app; agents can auto-restart, start with the app and keep the machine awake while turns run.
how: The desktop managed_agents module owns lifecycle (process_lifecycle, runtime, reconcile, restore, readiness); BackendKind is Local or Provider{id,config}; agent, persona and team definitions sync as relay events (kinds 30175, 30176, 30177); macOS power assertion while turns run.
verevonRelevance: Closest analogue to a Grok-style personal agent, but it lives on the user's machine and dies with it; Verevon should host personal agents server-side in sandboxes and borrow only the lifecycle states and owner controls.
notes: Presence is separate from process state (docs/agent-availability.md).

name: Persona and team library with a community catalog and snapshot sharing
what: A persona (name, avatar, prompt, model, runtime, triggers) is a reusable blueprint; teams group personas; both can be shared to a community catalog or sent to a person as a snapshot.
how: kind 30175 persona and 30176 team events are author-only unless a shared tag is set; kind 30178 team catalog embeds member projections so a shared team hydrates atomically and never leaks env vars, allowlist keys or paths; PersonaShareDialog sends a snapshot over DM or clipboard with a memory-share level; CommunityCatalogDialog browses shared items; NIP-AP also defines kind 44300 instruction version history.
verevonRelevance: Verevon org agent registry exists but has no sharing model; private-by-default, sanitized projections with atomic team share are good rules.
notes: NIP-PMA (kind 30179 owner-encrypted aggregate) is reserved and relays reject it today.

name: Agent cards: shareable PNG with an embedded snapshot
what: An agent can be minted as a trading-card style PNG that carries a verified snapshot and can be imported elsewhere.
how: Mint, load, list and save commands; the PNG embeds the snapshot and is round-trip verified; image generation uses an OpenAI key (INF, medium confidence on the generator).
verevonRelevance: A playful distribution format; low relevance for Verevon.

name: Add an agent or a whole team to a channel like adding a person
what: From the channel, pick a persona or team, choose runtime and model, or tap a quick-add avatar; the agent joins with a bot role and starts.
how: AddChannelBotDialog with personas, teams and generic sections, reuse detection, QuickBotBar (recent personas shown on hover), drag-drop via useQuickBotDrop, AddTeamToChannelDialog, WelcomeAgentCreateDialog for the first agent.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agent tab offers add existing or create; quick add, team add and drag-drop make multi-agent rooms practical.

name: Mentioning a sleeping agent wakes it (publish-first with replay floor)
what: @mentioning a stopped agent starts it, your message is sent first, and the agent processes the triggering message even though it started late.
how: The send flow readies mentioned agents, queues detached wakes and flushes them only after the relay accepts the publish; the harness gets BUZZ_ACP_REPLAY_FLOOR (clamped to 15 minutes) so the first REQ replays past the message; lazy pool connects and subscribes before spawning the model subprocess and can re-sleep after idle.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agents are model invocations so there is no wake race, but sandbox-backed agents with cold starts will need the same publish-first plus replay-floor discipline.
notes: Complexity is high because desktop-hosted agents can be offline; a server-hosted design avoids most of it.

name: Who may talk to an agent: owner-only default, allowlist, anyone, nobody, plus same-owner siblings
what: Each agent only responds to authors it admits: its owner by default, a list, everyone, or nobody (proactive only); agents with the same owner trust each other.
how: RespondTo enum (owner-only default, allowlist, anyone, nobody) enforced by the harness author gate; a sibling cache resolves same-owner agents via profile ownership with bounded retry for indeterminate lookups; desktop RespondToField and EditRespondToDialog edit it per agent and per channel.
verevonRelevance: Verevon bindings gate on trigger_modes and approval_mode but not on who may address an agent; an owner-only default is the right safe posture for personal agents placed in shared rooms.
notes: Default subscribe mode is mentions, so agents only wake on explicit @mentions unless configured otherwise (config.rs:334).

name: Mid-turn steering: new messages re-prompt a working agent instead of waiting
what: Message an agent while it is working and it folds your text into the task; alternatives queue the message, supersede the task, or interrupt only for the owner.
how: MultipleEventHandling: steer (default) cancels and re-prompts with the new events framed as arrived while working; queue waits; interrupt supersedes; owner-interrupt cancels only for the owner. Edited mentions also steer running turns and wake agents.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has a mid-stream queue endpoint; copy the framing semantics (steer vs supersede) and the owner-only interrupt policy.
notes: Four explicit policies is a strong, rare design.

name: Per-channel, per-thread and per-task agent sessions
what: An agent holds one independent conversation context per channel (threads share it by default, DMs are one conversation), can isolate sessions per thread, and can run one-shot task sessions; core memory and workspace are shared across sessions.
how: SessionPolicy channel (default) or thread; at most one prompt in flight per channel with queued batches; context_message_limit fetches 12 recent thread or DM messages by default; isolated_execution spawns a fresh process for a local task with deadline and cancel; session model notes are injected into the prompt so the agent knows it is one of several sessions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon turns every post into a separate thread; Buzz's channel-scoped context with an explicit sibling-session notice shows the alternative when a room wants continuity.

name: Agent etiquette contract in the base system prompt
what: Built-in rules teach agents how to behave in a shared room: publish only what is worth knowing, always answer a human, never send bare acknowledgements, mention the delegator when finished, avoid narrative mentions, resume silently after compaction, narrate progress because tool calls are invisible.
how: base_prompt.md is injected by the harness every turn: incoming-turn contract with structured sections, mention formatting rules (exact display name, no bold), callback mention rule, threading rule (flat for humans, nested allowed for agent-only work), and agent memory hygiene.
verevonRelevance: Verevon rooms with several agents will hit the same loops and noise; this text came from real failures and is directly reusable as a platform-level prompt layer.
notes: Loop avoidance is prompt-level only: the relay does apply per-principal message quotas (agent standard tier defaults to 120 per minute, crates/buzz-auth/src/rate_limit.rs:105) but no hop or loop-depth limit exists.

name: Agents speak only by explicit publish; reasoning is private to the owner
what: An agent's model text is not the message: it posts to the room through a tool or CLI call, so the room sees deliberate messages while thoughts and tool calls stay in the owner's transcript.
how: buzz-agent's default system prompt says tool calls are the only output; base prompt says reasoning and tool calls are invisible to humans and must be narrated; typing indicators and the working signal show activity without content.
verevonRelevance: Verevon streams each turn into the room; consider a publish-explicitly mode and a room-visible working summary so shared rooms are not flooded by agent monologues.
notes: Trade-off: no token streaming inside the room; users cannot watch an answer form.

name: Owner-only live transcript of an agent session (observer frames)
what: Owners open any of their agents' sessions and watch messages, thoughts, plans, tool calls, file edits with diffs, shell commands, permission events and errors, with a raw protocol rail; other members only see what the agent posts.
how: NIP-AO ephemeral kind 24200 frames, NIP-44 encrypted agent to owner, relay verifies the owner relation and never stores or audits them; clients keep an 800-event ring buffer; local agents use an in-process observer; the desktop parses ACP read/write frames into twelve render classes, classifies tool calls (shell, file edit, buzz CLI operations) into semantic cards, and can archive frames locally. Mobile has an agent activity sheet.
verevonRelevance: The most important gap in the Verevon room: show the owner (and optionally the room) what the agent is doing in verb-object-outcome cards instead of a status line; also decide deliberately whether non-owners may see it.
notes: Best-in-class among the peers reviewed for owner transparency; weakness is owner-only (no shared view for teammates) and ephemerality means no relay-side history.

name: One unified agent-working signal with a liveness backstop
what: Every surface (sidebar channel badges, profile, composer bar, tray) shows the same working state with elapsed time; a ping every ten seconds distinguishes a crashed turn from a slow one.
how: agentWorkingSignal merges observer-derived active turns (primary) with bot typing indicators (fallback for remote harnesses without relay observer); BUZZ_ACP_TURN_LIVENESS_SECS defaults to 10; TurnLivenessIndicator and BotActivityBar render it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon pulse reads thread status from a 6 s poll; a single derived working signal with a crash backstop avoids inconsistent badges.

name: Owner control frames: cancel a turn, switch model live
what: Owners can interrupt a running turn and change the model or effort for a live session from the transcript or channel header.
how: NIP-AO control frames (cancel_turn per channel) encrypted owner to agent; the desktop also dispatches control_result frames for model switches and stores captured session config options; canInterruptTurn flags which agents can be interrupted.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has cancel and steer for runs; per-session model switching from the room is an extra owner control.
notes: NIP text defines only cancel_turn; code shows more control results (medium confidence on full set).

name: Tool permissions are auto-approved by the harness; no human approval gate
what: There is no interactive approve or deny UI for agent tool calls; the harness answers every permission request itself and the desktop only displays permission events.
how: handle_permission_request picks the allow_once option automatically (falls back to reject_once if none) and logs auto-approving; the only gating is the harness permission mode (default, auto, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, dontAsk, plan) for runtimes that support it; buzz-agent asks per MCP call but a comment in permission.rs cites a BUZZ_ACP_PERMISSION_POLICY that does not exist.
verevonRelevance: Corrects the scout, which listed human approval of tool calls: Verevon's approval_mode and awaiting_approval cards are ahead; Buzz's real human-in-the-loop lives in owner-reviewed proposals, not tool gating.
notes: Code is ground truth; the documented policy env var is absent.

name: Owner-reviewed proposals delivered over a private agent-to-owner channel
what: An agent can propose creating or editing an agent or adding a project channel; the proposal reaches only the owner as a prefilled dialog and nothing changes until the owner saves.
how: CLI agents draft-create and draft-update (require BUZZ_AUTH_TAG) and projects add-channel emit typed requests inside the encrypted observer channel; the desktop parses them (parseAgentManagementRequest, parseProjectChannelRequest) with a strict allowlisted schema, id dedupe and a 100-request queue cap; the agent is told never to claim the thing exists until the owner approves.
verevonRelevance: Matches the Verevon rule that the Model proposes and another plane executes; a typed proposal sent to the accountable human with an explicit confirm is a clean pattern and could also be the missing resume path for approvals.
notes: Scope is narrow (agents and project channels), not general action approval.

name: In-room setup nudge card when an agent cannot run
what: If an agent is missing a key, CLI login, adapter or config, it posts a chat message with an interactive card telling the owner what to fix; clients without cards show plain prose.
how: buzz-acp setup_mode appends a fenced buzz:config-nudge JSON sentinel (agent name, pubkey, typed requirements such as env_key, cli_login, adapter_missing, git_bash, missing_binary) to a kind 9 body; the desktop strips it and renders ConfigNudgeCard only when the signer matches the named agent, with Doctor and Edit-agent actions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agents that fail on missing connectors or credentials could post a structured, signer-checked card instead of an error line; sentinel-in-markdown degrades safely.

name: Agent memory: owner-readable engrams, core memory in every turn, graph viewer
what: Each agent keeps a small core memory that is injected into every turn and cold memories linked by wiki links; the owner can browse them as a tree from core with orphans and dangling links.
how: NIP-AE kind 30174, NIP-44 encrypted to the agent-owner conversation key (so the owner can always read), d-tags HMACed so slugs stay private; buzz mem ls/get/set/patch/rm/hash; core fetched per session (engram_fetch.rs), prompt tells agents to keep core under about 10 KB (hard limit 65,535 bytes) and to ask the owner before evicting or removing memory; desktop MemorySection uses buildMemoryGraph.
verevonRelevance: Verevon memory scopes have no space scope; Buzz scopes memory per agent and owner pair, not per room, which creates cross-room leakage risk (the information-flow draft proposes audience labels); pick the scope deliberately.
notes: Memory is human-auditable by construction, a strong trust feature.

name: Nest: persistent agent workspace with conventions
what: A shared folder gives every agent orientation, plans, research, work logs and an outbox that persist across sessions, with repos linked in.
how: First-launch creation of GUIDES, RESEARCH, PLANS, WORK_LOGS, OUTBOX and .scratch plus an AGENTS.md and a buzz-cli SKILL.md refreshed on template version change; per-harness skill directory symlinks.
verevonRelevance: Analogous to Verevon durable Space workspace; adopt the conventional folder layout and an AGENTS.md orientation file.

name: Proactive agent work: heartbeat prompts, workflow schedules, recovery wake
what: Agents can be prompted on a timer, woken by workflow schedules, and re-woken after a quiet host respawn.
how: BUZZ_ACP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL and prompt (off by default), cron workflows, recovery_wake for respawns and queued retries; respond-to nobody gives a proactive-only agent.
verevonRelevance: Verevon schedules are richer (Control decision per fire) but creation lives in Settings; a simple heartbeat plus nobody mode covers proactive agents in rooms.

name: Agent lifetime bounds and remote self-reaping
what: Agents cap turn duration, turns per session and idle time; a remote agent shuts itself down after hours of silence and on a relay message, because the desktop keeps no control channel after launch.
how: BUZZ_ACP_MAX_TURN_DURATION, MAX_TURNS_PER_SESSION, EXIT_AFTER_INACTIVITY; remote spec states five invariants (identity fail-closed, no secrets in configuration, presence-is-status, at-most-one-live-instance, intentional-termination-is-final); presence is a lease renewed by the agent.
verevonRelevance: The presence-is-a-lease and self-reaping principles apply to Verevon sandboxes that must not bill forever.

name: Remote agents through provider binaries (Kubernetes first)
what: The desktop can deploy an agent onto remote infrastructure through a swappable provider binary; the same agent identity resumes later on a new body.
how: Zero-registration plugin contract for executables named buzz-backend-<id> (discovery, info, deploy), a bare Pod running the sprig all-in-one image, immutable per-attempt secrets, no service-account token; status, steering and shutdown flow only over the relay.
verevonRelevance: Closest Buzz analogue to a hosted agent PC, but explicitly has no sandbox beyond a Pod and a key as a Secret; Verevon sandbox-manager leases are stronger.
notes: VISION.md marks it spec in review; code exists but production readiness is unproven (medium confidence).

name: Persistent agent address lock (talk to an agent without re-mentioning it)
what: After a person mentions an agent in a thread or composer, the agent stays addressed: later messages implicitly mention it, the composer shows its avatar next to the @ button, and one click (or turning the preference off) releases it. A shortcut (Cmd or Ctrl plus Shift plus M) toggles the default agent.
how: persistentAgentAudience is a module-level store keyed by owner:channel:composer scope (capped at 200 scopes, ordered, with a revision counter and per-scope exclusion set); useAutoPinMentionedAgents promotes mentioned agents with a 4-second confirmation popover that offers Turn off; the synthesized leading mention prefix is captured as provenance so edits and drafts can strip exactly what was generated (stripImplicitAgentMentionPrefix); threads inherit the audience through useThreadAgentAudience; a Settings toggle keeps mentioned agents pinned.
verevonRelevance: Verevon posts always reach the model, so the problem is inverted there; once Spaces allow human-to-human chat, an explicit per-composer agent lock is the clean way to hold a running conversation with one agent inside a mixed room.
notes: The audience store is in memory (no localStorage in the module), so a restart drops the lock while the Settings preference persists (medium confidence on persistence of the lock itself).

name: Chat-native multi-agent coordination (orchestrator by @mention; typed job kinds stay unused)
what: A team of agents cooperates by talking in a channel: an orchestrator persona posts a plan, dispatches teammates by name, and reports results. There is no task graph, queue or delegation protocol that the platform enforces.
how: The example pack meadow-core defines an orchestrator (Skip) whose prompt says never to build, plus reviewer personas; BUZZ_ACP_TEAM_INSTRUCTIONS injects shared team text into every member prompt; kinds 43001-43006 (job request, accepted, progress, result, cancel, error) exist in the kind registry and are read only by the home feed query, while buzz-acp publishes ordinary kind 9 messages; VISION_PROJECTS lists a coding agent that watches job kind 43001 as designed, not built.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs delegation between room agents; Buzz shows that chat-only coordination works for demos but leaves no durable, queryable unit of work, so keep Verevon runs and subagent records as the delegation backbone and render them in the room.
notes: Corrects the scout, which listed the job kinds as live coordination.

name: Agent subscription rules and trigger modes (mentions, all, rule file with evalexpr filters)
what: Each agent decides which room events wake it: only explicit @mentions (default), every message, or an ordered rule list scoped per channel with kinds, a require-mention flag and a boolean content filter; persona files add keywords and an all-messages switch.
how: SubscribeMode enum (Mentions, All, Config) in buzz-acp config; filter.rs builds an evalexpr context from the event (content, author, kind, channel, timestamp) and evaluates rules first-match-wins with a hard timeout and length cap; persona frontmatter carries triggers (keywords, all_messages) and lifecycle hooks (on_start, on_message).
verevonRelevance: Verevon binding trigger_modes are a small enum; a rule list with a bounded expression filter would let one agent serve several rooms with different wake rules.

name: ACP harness: process pool, per-scope queues, batching and crash recovery
what: Agent runtimes run as supervised subprocesses behind a harness that receives room events, batches what arrived while the agent was busy, prompts the agent once per batch, and respawns it if it crashes.
how: buzz-acp holds a pool of 1-32 ACP subprocesses with a claim and return lifecycle (the client is not Clone, ownership moves out on claim); queue.rs keeps per-session-scope queues (cap 500 per scope, aggregate cap per channel), drains all pending events for the oldest channel into one prompt, and offers Drop or Queue dedup; a poisoned agent is respawned; the harness persists no state.
verevonRelevance: A Verevon room with several agents needs the same bounded-queue and batch discipline so a burst of messages does not launch one run per post.
notes: About 3,100 lines of relay client, 2,565 of queue and 2,253 of pool per ARCHITECTURE.md; sizeable for a harness.

name: Self-summarizing context handoff with a bounded recovery ladder
what: When an agent's conversation approaches the model's context window it summarizes its own history, resets, and continues; if the provider rejects a request for size it retries through a rescue ladder instead of failing the turn.
how: handoff.rs generates a plain-text summary (original task, accomplishments, decisions, remaining work, one next step) under an 8,192-token cap, counts every attempt against BUZZ_AGENT_MAX_HANDOFFS (default 10) so a flaky summarizer cannot loop, and a reactive ladder (MAX_CONTEXT_RECOVERIES_PER_RUN = 3) handles provider context errors; a _PostCompact hook restores context after compaction.
verevonRelevance: Long-lived Verevon room agents will hit context limits; bound the number of compactions per run and count failed attempts as spent budget, as Buzz does.

name: Provider-agnostic agent LLM client with thinking-effort normalization
what: One agent binary talks to Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Databricks (serving endpoints and AI Gateway v2) and OpenRouter; a single effort setting is clamped to what each model supports.
how: Provider enum with per-provider wire builders (Databricks uses OAuth PKCE or a static token); BUZZ_AGENT_THINKING_EFFORT (none to max) is translated per model with warnings when clamped or omitted; prompt caching toggle; desktop discovers models per provider and exposes model and effort pickers.
verevonRelevance: Verevon routes through Model Gateway so this layer is not needed, but the clamp-and-warn pattern for an effort control that spans models is reusable in the room model picker.

name: Agent secrets: reserved-key fence, per-agent env editor and OS keyring custody
what: Users can add environment variables to an agent but cannot override the keys that carry its identity, relay URL, run command or security gates; agent signing keys sit in the operating-system keyring rather than in files.
how: One canonical RESERVED_ENV_KEYS list is include!d into both build.rs (compile-time rejection of baked collisions) and env_vars.rs (save-time validation and spawn-time filtering) so the two cannot drift; reserved groups are identity and secrets, relay URL, code-execution surface and security gates (respond-to mode and allowlists); the SecretStore keeps one keychain blob per process with a plaintext 0o600 fallback; SECURITY.md documents migration that never resurrects rotated keys.
verevonRelevance: Verevon keeps agent secrets out of browsers by design; the single shared reserved-key list used at build, save and spawn time is a pattern for any user-editable agent configuration.
notes: Keys live on the user's machine, which Verevon avoids by hosting agents server-side.

name: Agent turn metrics with local archive (no budget cap or spend UI in the OSS build)
what: Each completed agent turn publishes an encrypted token and cost record readable only by the owner, and the desktop archives those records locally; there is no per-agent budget, limit or cost chart in the OSS client.
how: NIP-AM kind 44200 is NIP-44 encrypted to the owner with p and agent tags, published by the harness on TurnCompletionGuard in pool.rs (usage.rs); the desktop decrypts and stores plaintext rows in a per-identity SQLite archive and exposes get_agent_usage_series; the React hook named in the bridge comment (useAgentUsageSeries) does not exist in this tree, and no cap enforcement code was found.
