verevonRelevance: Verevon cost-core has org budgets but no per-Space or per-agent view; the owner-encrypted per-turn record is a privacy-preserving model, but ship the budget and display parts Buzz lacks.
notes: Medium confidence: the usage UI may live in a non-OSS build; the OSS tree only shows the data path.

name: Verb-object-outcome tool-call cards with a raw-event floor
what: Agent activity is rendered as one-line sentences (for example Edited a file, Ran tests, Sent a message to a channel) that expand to arguments and diffs, with failures prominent, reads quiet, and an always-available raw rail.
how: A provider chain (load-skill, developer-harness, Buzz CLI) classifies each tool call into render classes (message, relay-op, file-edit, file-read, skill-read, image, shell, status, thought, plan, permission, error, generic, raw-rail, suppressed); the same card renders whether the agent posted via MCP or a buzz shell command; running rows mutate in place; references resolve to channel and person names; unknown tools degrade to a truthful generic row; ToolItem, ShellCommandBlock, TodoToolSummary, FileEditDiffView and SentMessageContextDialog implement the cards.
verevonRelevance: The strongest design text in the repo for the supervision problem; Verevon should adopt the verb-object-outcome frame and the never-go-dark rule for run and approval cards in rooms.
notes: Owner-only today (see observer record), so teammates never see these cards. Grok Bot narrates agent work similarly but with approvals; Buzz has no approval cards.

name: Availability is conversational presence; unknown is never shown as offline
what: An agent's status dot means it can be talked to, not that a process exists; a failed or pending read shows unknown, and deleting or starting an agent never assumes a remote body is gone.
how: Presence comes only from signed kind 20001 snapshots for the exact requested keys; no entry means Offline only for keys in the snapshot; a locally stopped record with live presence disables Start with an explanation; shutdown is a request, not a confirmed termination; policy-only discovery carries status unknown through IPC; e2e tests hold the IPC read pending to prove it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Space presence rows and any agent status chips should adopt the three-valued status (online, offline, unknown) and never infer offline from a failed read.
notes: The doc itself states the Start guard is not a distributed singleton lock.

name: Exact-key agent identity: a persona is a template, an instance is the member
what: Opening an agent from a message, member list, DM or link always shows that exact agent; shared personas never alias a different running copy, and a marker shows when an owned agent is not managed on this device.
how: useCanonicalManagedAgentProfile and resolveCanonicalManagedAgent resolve by exact pubkey; persona navigation is a separate path that picks an archive-aware representative; no synthetic secretless ManagedAgent record is created; one shared KnownAgentPubkeysProvider supplies inventory so rows never create their own queries.
verevonRelevance: Verevon bindings link an agent definition to a Control subject; keeping instance identity distinct from the reusable definition prevents a message from one agent opening another's controls.

name: Mention-to-invite: addressing an owned agent that is not yet in the channel
what: When you @mention one of your agents that is not a member of the room, the composer offers Invite (add it, then send) or reference-only send; a vanished or revoked agent fails visibly and keeps the draft.
how: Owned agents are discovered from owner-signed kind 30177 records plus verified NIP-OA profile envelopes (membership from the latest kind 39002 snapshot); the picker may admit non-members but publication separately refreshes authorization for the exact destination, including a newly created DM; each Invite owns a pending latch and abort signal across preparation, adds and publication.
verevonRelevance: Verevon personal agents must be draftable into rooms with explicit consent from their owner; the rule that picker evidence never authorizes publication fits the Control-decision model.
notes: Docs call for independent security review before landing; the atomicity gap between final authorization and publish is acknowledged.

name: Product-behavior benchmark for agents in rooms (buzz-dataset on a Harbor adapter)
what: A suite of tasks grades how an agent behaves inside Buzz, not just whether it solves a problem: replies in the right thread, notifies exactly the intended person, does not wake agents named in narrative, keeps simultaneous requests isolated, retrieves cold memory.
how: benchmarks/buzz-dataset has ten Harbor tasks tagged Regression or Workflow; harbor-buzz-orchestra runs the real buzz-acp, buzz-agent and buzz-dev-mcp process tree against the production relay and Postgres inside each task container, with a manifest-defined roster, byte-pinned prompts and per-trial keys; verifiers grade the exported relay snapshot; some graded behaviors are deliberately absent from the task text so they must come from the base prompt.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should build the same regression suite for room behavior (right thread, right recipient, no cross-room leakage, no wake on narrative mentions) because model or prompt changes silently break these contracts.
notes: Regression results are reported per behavior, not averaged; copy that rule.

name: Buzz Mesh: relay-gated shared model compute (optional build feature)
what: Community members can opt in to serve a local model; teammates' agents use it through a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with membership as the only gate and a consent screen that says prompts run on other people's hardware.
how: Desktop mesh_llm module (about 4,600 lines: coordinator, discovery, recovery, transport policy, catalog, usage) built on the external mesh-llm SDK behind a cargo feature; relay membership gates discovery; share toggle and serving-usage UI in features/mesh-compute; the built-in Fizz agent path is Desktop to buzz-acp to buzz-agent to MeshLLM.
verevonRelevance: Not relevant to a hosted product, but the pattern of reusing room membership as the admission gate for a second resource (compute) is the same idea as Space membership gating sandboxes.
notes: Feature-flagged at build time; the dev runbook refers to a mesh-enabled branch, so default builds may not include it.

name: [Not built] Agent browser or computer use, hosted agent PC, per-tool approvals and spend caps
what: Buzz agents get a shell, file tools and the buzz CLI on the owner's machine or in a bare Pod; there is no browser, no desktop control, no managed cloud computer, no human approval of tool calls and no budget limit.
how: buzz-dev-mcp exposes only shell, read_file, view_image, str_replace and todo; grep of crates found no browser automation (only OAuth headless-login strings); the harness auto-selects allow_once for every permission request; remote agents run in a Pod with the key as a Secret and no further sandbox.
verevonRelevance: This is the biggest gap between Buzz and Grok Bot and Verevon: Verevon sandbox leases, Quarry browser grants and approval modes are ahead of Buzz here; do not borrow from Buzz for agent PC, browser or approvals.
notes: Absence established by grep and tool-list reading (medium confidence).

name: Channel canvas: one Markdown document per channel with history, diff and restore
what: Each channel has a shared Markdown document reachable from the channel details sheet; members edit it in a text box, see rendered Markdown, browse every past revision with a line diff, and restore an older one. Agents read and write it through the CLI.
how: Every save is a signed kind 40100 event (full replacement); the newest event is the head; CanvasHistoryPanel lists all revisions newest first, diffs the selected one against the head with the diff package, and restore republishes old content as a new head; buzz canvas get, set, history and restore mirror the UI. The editor is a plain Textarea, not a rich-text or real-time collaborative editor.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no Space-authored document; a per-room Markdown canvas with append-only history and restore is the cheapest shared artifact, but build real co-editing if Spaces need Notion or Slack-canvas parity.
notes: Slack and Teams offer richer co-authored canvases and wikis; Buzz's value is the audit-friendly revision stream and agent write access, not the editor.

name: Canvas write safety: expected-revision precondition checked by the relay
what: If two people edit the canvas at once, the second save is rejected with a clear reload message, or, if it landed first, the loser's text stays in History so nothing is lost.
how: A save carries an expected-revision tag (head event id or the literal none); the desktop precondition-checks the head, stamps created_at above the head, and verifies after write; the relay parses the tag and calls insert_canvas_head_checked, returning conflict strings for missing, mismatched or non-superseding heads; clients set a consistency strong extension so the read that gates the write hits the writer, never a replica; future-timestamp ceilings stop a poisoned head from freezing the document.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon shared artifact needs compare-and-set on a head revision enforced server-side; the pre-write, post-write and unverified-notice states are a good template for honest conflict UX.
notes: The desktop comment still says full linearization is phase 2, but the relay now enforces the checked insert; the client keeps both layers.

name: Channel artifacts (NIP-AR): typed editable records governed by channel access
what: A relay-level primitive for editable work records (tasks, project cards) that live in a channel or thread, with revisions, move, delete and restore, and read access identical to the channel.
how: Kind 45010 events carry a complete snapshot with ar, d (stable UUID), h (home channel), type, title, op (create, update, move, delete, restore) and prev tags; the relay advances the head atomically in artifact_heads and rejects a stale prev as a conflict, so timestamps never decide; current-state queries match client-defined tags with AND and OR rules under enforced size and time budgets; revisions never count as chat unread or repeat mention notifications; only server tests and an SDK builder use it, no desktop or mobile UI emits 45010.
verevonRelevance: A generic record type whose access is the room's access (and whose edits never create chat noise) is exactly the missing Space task or decision object; copy the prev-based compare-and-set and the tag-query contract.
notes: Backend only; no client consumes it yet, so product value is unproven.

name: Relay-hosted git with refs on object storage and a formal safety spec
what: The same domain serves git clone and push over smart HTTP with channel-bound permissions and signed identities; repositories survive pod loss because refs and packs live in object storage.
how: crates/buzz-relay/src/api/git (about 15,000 lines: transport, hydrate, manifest, pack cache, CAS publish, policy hook, settings) implements smart HTTP; docs/git-on-object-storage.md states axioms and three theorems (durability ordering, manifest reconstruction, linearizable refs) with a TLA+ model; HMAC-secured internal policy callback; NIP-34 repo announcements carry buzz- tags.
verevonRelevance: Out of scope for a chat Space, but it shows an unusual rigor bar (spec, model checking, conformance table) for any Verevon durable-state plane such as Space deletion receipts.

name: Branch protection driven by channel role and ref patterns
what: Repository owners protect refs so only certain roles may push, force pushes and deletes are blocked, or a ref can change only through a reviewed patch.
how: The permission model is channel role equals repo role; buzz-protect tags on the kind 30617 announcement add per-pattern rules (push:<role>, no-force-push, no-delete, require-patch) with a safe pattern grammar (refs/ prefix, at most three single-segment wildcards, 50 rules); bots are promoted to member and an agent managed by the repository owner is treated as the owner; unknown rules are skipped with a warning. The vision text describes push-allowed lists and a require-approval count that the code does not implement.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Space-level rules where room role determines what an agent may do to a bound resource; inheriting the resource role from the room role removes a second ACL.
notes: Doc-vs-code drift: approvals as a merge gate are designed, not enforced.

name: Projects: multi-repo grouping, project home channel and project sidebar
what: A project groups repositories from several owners under one card with its own home channel, listed or unlisted visibility, a code browser and an activity digest, and appears in the sidebar for members.
how: kind 30621 (NIP-MP) is a single-signer replaceable event listing repo coordinates plus buzz-channel binding; the signer gets no authority over member repos, so push policy reads each repo event; desktop features/projects (about 280 files including tests) implement creation, repo attach, sidebar membership sync, home channel healing and share links; Projects is preview-gated.
verevonRelevance: Verevon project and case Spaces that group several resources can follow the one-signer, no-authority-over-members rule so a Space never widens an owner plane ACL.
notes: The grouping rule is elegant but only matters for cross-owner git repos.

name: Issues and work items on NIP-34 with categories, labels and assignments
what: Projects list issues and change requests per repository, with Issue, Change request and Improvement categories, labels, assignees, comment timelines and status.
how: NIP-34 kinds 1621 (issue) and 1630-1633 (status) plus assignment events; category is derived from labels (projectTaskCategoryFromLabels); fetchProjectsWorkItems aggregates with bounded relay fan-out and reports failed sections (assignments, comments, PR updates, statuses) without discarding root items; CLI buzz issues create, get, list, status, assign.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no Space task list; the partial-failure-aware aggregate (named failed sections instead of an empty list) matches the unavailable[] contract already in the Space BFF.
notes: No kanban or board view; it is a list-and-detail tracker. Linear or GitHub Issues are far richer.

name: Pull requests with review requests, approvals and desktop-side merge
what: A change can be proposed, review is requested from named people, approvals and change requests appear on the PR, and the owner merges from a button; conflicts offer a prepared terminal recovery.
how: NIP-34 kinds 1618 and 1619 for PRs and updates; reviews are labeled kind 1 comments (review-request, approval, changes-requested) trusted only when signed by the PR author or repo owner; status kinds 1630-1633 are signed with the repo owner key; merge_project_pull_request runs git merge and push on the desktop under the owner identity, then publishes a merged status; conflict recovery opens a terminal at a prepared checkout.
verevonRelevance: The review-as-signed-comment trust rule (only author or owner may change status) is a reusable approval-provenance idea; merging on a client machine is not.
notes: Merge executes client-side, so it needs the owner's key and a local checkout; a server-side merge train is still designed only.

name: Branch as channel: creating a branch creates a conversation
what: Creating a remote branch from the UI can create a channel bound to it so discussion, review and status of that branch have a home.
how: create_project_remote_branch pushes the ref and the project channel creation flow binds a channel via the buzz-channel tag; useBindProjectRepositoryChannel and ProjectChannelHome render it; archive-on-merge is stated in VISION_PROJECTS but no archive-on-merge code path was verified.
verevonRelevance: The idea of a resource that auto-spawns its own room (a run, case or document gets a thread-space) maps to Verevon case and project Spaces.
notes: Medium confidence: the archive-on-merge half is documented intent only.

name: In-page agent chat with selected context, untrusted-data framing and pre-send disclosure
what: On a project, file or work-item page a side chat lets you ask an agent about what you are looking at; the page selection becomes context, and a preview shows the exact text that will be appended to your message before it is signed.
how: projectDetailAgentContextBlock builds a hidden footer from project, repo, branch, file and selected items (caps of 100 items and 16,000 characters); untrustedPromptValue collapses control characters and JSON-quotes every relay- or git-controlled value; a fixed notice tells the agent to treat quoted values as data; AgentContextPayloadPreview shows the byte-identical payload pre-send because post-send disclosure is not a trust boundary; the conversation is a DM with the chosen agent, restored only from a pointer this feature stored.
verevonRelevance: Directly applicable to Spaces where a page, document or run is passed as context to an agent: quote untrusted metadata, tell the model it is data, and show the user exactly what will be sent.
notes: Strong injection hygiene at the prompt boundary; it does not solve injection (the notice is advisory).

name: Git identity for agents: Nostr-signed commits and credential helper
what: Agents commit and push as themselves: commits and tags are signed with the agent's Nostr key through git's signing program interface, and pushes authenticate with a per-request signature instead of a stored password.
how: git-sign-nostr implements the gpg.x509.program contract for BIP-340 Schnorr signatures (NIP-GS); git-credential-nostr answers git credential requests with NIP-98 HTTP auth events; the relay maps the signer to an owner through NIP-OA for push policy.
verevonRelevance: Relevant only if Verevon agents push code to hosted repos; the pattern of no stored credential, per-request signature is the same one Quarry grants aim at.

name: In-app terminal docked to a channel with context injection and an environment allowlist
what: A docked or maximized terminal panel opens next to a channel or thread, with the channel, thread, identity and relay exposed as environment variables so scripts and the buzz CLI act on what you are looking at.
how: Alacritty-based terminal engine in a separate crate (grid, parser, damage encoding) with a portable-pty child; env_fence clears the inherited environment and rebuilds from an allowlist (HOME, USER, LANG and a few more) because a denylist once leaked the nsec; context.rs validates the channel name against a conservative character class and substitutes the UUID rather than stripping, to defeat shell injection through prompt expansion.
verevonRelevance: A human-side terminal tied to a Space is a power-user feature for later; the allowlist-not-denylist and validate-then-substitute rules apply to any Verevon sandbox or script that receives room-controlled strings.
notes: Marketed as Buzz Term in the channel header; unclear how much of it is gated for the OSS build (button is visible in the header code).

name: Agent-visible shared knowledge: Nest workspace and memory, with crystallization only planned
what: Durable shared knowledge today is agent-side (engrams and the Nest folder) and the canvas; the planned AI-proposes, human-approves summary that pins as an artifact is not built.
how: Knowledge Crystallization appears in VISION.md as planned culture feature; the shipped pieces are NIP-AE engrams, the Nest conventions and canvases; search is plain FTS.
verevonRelevance: The propose-then-approve pin flow is the right shape for Verevon Space knowledge but must be built; Buzz offers only the vision.

name: [Not built] Task board, file library, wiki and polls as room artifacts
what: There is no kanban or checklist board, no per-channel files tab or drive, no wiki, and no native polls; attachments stay inside messages.
how: No board or files-library route in desktop/src/app/routes.ts; media is addressed by hash inside messages; polls are listed as planned; the only list-like work surface is the project issue list.
verevonRelevance: Both products lack these Slack and Teams staples (Lists, Files tab, Wiki); NIP-AR is Buzz's unused foundation for them.
notes: Absence established by route and kind inspection (medium confidence).

name: Push realtime over authenticated WebSocket with bounded per-connection loops
what: Every client holds one WebSocket that delivers new messages, typing and presence the moment they are accepted; slow or dead clients are dropped rather than allowed to back up the server.
how: NIP-01 EVENT, REQ, EOSE and CLOSED frames on /; a per-connection sequence of host-to-community binding, semaphore admission, NIP-42 challenge, then three loops (receive, send with a bounded channel, 30-second ping with three missed pongs to disconnect); a slow client that fills its buffer three times in a row is cancelled; 1,024 subscriptions per connection and a 1,024-permit handler semaphore cap work; rejections travel on the frame's own acknowledgement (OK or CLOSED), never a bare NOTICE.
verevonRelevance: Verevon polls every 6 seconds; a push channel with bounded loops and per-frame rejection addressing is the minimum for typing, presence and agent activity in rooms.
notes: The Nostr wire format is a protocol-first choice Verevon should not copy; the connection discipline is what transfers.

name: Three-tier subscription fan-out that never leaks private channels
what: A message is delivered only to connections subscribed to that channel and authorized for it, and a catch-all subscription never receives private-channel events.
how: SubscriptionRegistry keeps DashMap indexes by (channel, kind), by channel, and a linear tier for global subscriptions; global subscriptions are excluded from channel-scoped events as a security boundary; the REQ handler checks accessible channels before registering so a non-member cannot receive live events in the gap; kinds [] means match nothing.
verevonRelevance: Space fan-out must authorize on subscribe and index by room; the register-after-authorize ordering is the detail that prevents the classic race.

name: Community-scoped Redis bus, measured at a 64x ingress reduction
what: Cluster nodes only receive the traffic of communities they actually serve, so adding tenants does not multiply every node's load.
how: Redis pub/sub topics are buzz:{community}:channel:{id} and buzz:{community}:global with dynamic SUBSCRIBE on a dedicated connection, broadcast channel of 4,096 and reconnect with 1 to 30 second backoff; the perf harness proves 64 communities at 100 events per second drop from 6,400 to 100 events per second per pod and exits non-zero if the reduction falls below 95% of ideal; presence, typing, cache invalidation and connection-control use the same community prefix.
verevonRelevance: Verevon NATS subjects between planes should be tenant-scoped the same way and carry a regression test that turns red if a scoped subscriber starts receiving the global firehose.
notes: ARCHITECTURE.md still lists cross-node presence as future work, but the handler now publishes presence to the community global topic (crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/event.rs:989), so that doc line is stale.

name: Ingest pipeline with ordered side effects and atomic head writes
what: Posting a message verifies the signature, checks membership, stores it, publishes it to peers, fans it out, writes the audit entry and triggers workflows in a fixed order, and the sender is acknowledged only at the end.
how: Steps are auth, pubkey match, ephemeral routing, spawn_blocking signature verify, membership, DB insert (search tsvector generated in the same statement), Redis publish, local fan-out, then spawned audit and workflow triggers that cannot fail the write; replaceable and parameterized-replaceable kinds take atomic replace paths with stale-write protection; canvas and artifact writes use head-checked inserts under advisory locks.
verevonRelevance: A Space post path should likewise validate, authorize, persist, then fan out in a documented order with audit and automation as non-blocking tails.
notes: Audit and workflow fire-and-forget means a crash can lose an audit row for an accepted event (INF from the spawned-task design, medium confidence).

name: Relay-computed channel and thread windows with exact cursors (NIP-CW)
what: Channel timelines page by top-level messages (not raw events), with reply counts and participants attached, an exact has-more flag, and no duplicate or skipped rows when many messages share a second.
how: An HTTP /query extension (top_level, include_summaries, include_aux, until plus before_id composite cursor) served from thread_metadata computed at ingest; the relay returns relay-signed kind 39005 thread summaries and 39006 channel bounds (39007 for thread mode); generic Nostr clients ignore the fields and degrade to a normal query; the desktop channelWindowStore keeps authoritative pages, a live overlay and live summary registers that a page supersedes.
verevonRelevance: The best answer in the repo to the room timeline problem: server-computed top-level paging with exact cursors, which Verevon needs the moment rooms hold human chat and threads.
notes: Needed only because Nostr filters cannot express no-reply-tag; a native API would be simpler.

name: Read-your-writes discipline: writer pinned for decisions, replicas for display
what: Anything that decides a write or a permission is read from the primary database; scrolling, counts and badges may read a slightly stale replica.
how: Db::query_events always reads the writer; query_events_routed opts display reads into replica routing under a soundness predicate and a freshness budget; clients declare write-influencing reads with a consistency strong filter field that can only force the writer (any other value is a 400); a deferred commit-time constraint trigger keeps the created_at floor that makes replica cursor fences sound; a caller classification table must be updated with every new call site.
verevonRelevance: State the same rule in the Space BFF: reads that gate a Control decision or a write must hit the authority plane, display reads may use projections; the one-way consistency field prevents misuse.
notes: Plan doc status is active, so parts may still be in flight.

name: Native Rust WebSocket with 8 ms frame coalescing for the desktop webview
what: The desktop keeps the relay socket in native code and delivers incoming frames to the UI in small batches, so a catch-up burst does not freeze the interface.
how: tokio-tungstenite in the Tauri backend, one shared authenticated session per relay and identity multiplexing every subscription, frames coalesced for 8 ms into a JSON array capped at 7,680 serialized bytes to stay below Tauri's 8,192-byte direct-execute IPC threshold and avoid the slow callback path; NIP-42 handled in the shared buzz-ws-client crate.
verevonRelevance: Only relevant to a native shell, but it is a concrete example of measuring the transport-to-UI boundary and bounding batch size by serialized bytes rather than frame count.

name: Per-user preferences synced across devices as field-level last-writer-wins registers
what: Sidebar sections, stars, mutes, sort order and project membership follow you to every device, merge deterministically when two devices change different things, and do not overwrite remote data after a failed fetch.
how: Each preference is a NIP-78 kind 30078 blob (distinct d tags) encrypted to the user; the document is a tree of registers [version, device id, value] merged per leaf by (version, device bytes, tombstone, value bytes), so any two devices converge; a persisted per-key remote-head watermark blocks seed-publishing when a remote blob ever existed even if a fetch times out; found, absent and error are a tri-state.
verevonRelevance: Verevon stores per-user room preferences nowhere; a small LWW-register document per user and Space solves multi-device sorting, mutes and pins without server logic.
notes: Mutes and manual-unread overrides stay out of read frontiers by design (docs/buzz-v1-extension-design.md).

name: Desktop head-page cache as a paint accelerator, not an offline store
what: Recently opened channels paint instantly from a local cache and are then replaced by the relay's authoritative page; losing connectivity does not give a usable offline mode on desktop.
how: channel_head_cache.rs stores up to 32 channels per (identity, relay) scope in SQLite with a 1 MiB row cap and schema version, hydrated before subscribe and always superseded by the relay response; the separate local-save archive copies selected messages, observer frames and agent metrics into a per-identity SQLite file with retention.
verevonRelevance: A tiny head-page cache gives most of the perceived speed of offline apps for little complexity, and fits a polling-to-push migration for Spaces.
notes: The mobile spec demands offline-first, which the desktop does not implement.

name: Mobile offline-first contract: pending, sent and failed with no duplicate on retry
what: The mobile spec requires cached content immediately, reading and composing offline, drafts that survive updates, and distinct pending, sent and failed states where sent means the relay accepted it.
how: VISION_MOBILE.md states: events are verified once and folded into a derived store that can be discarded, uncommitted data lives in separate minimal stores, no blocking of the UI isolate, retry must not create duplicates, uncertain acceptance stays pending, and critical local actions such as leaving a community do not wait for the relay.
verevonRelevance: The sent-means-accepted and retry-without-duplicate wording is the right acceptance criteria for a Verevon Space composer once human messages exist.
notes: Spec priority over code: the document itself says not all intents are implemented.

name: Selective encryption: server-readable chat, NIP-44 for private blobs, no end-to-end channels
what: Channels and DMs are server-managed (so search, audit and eDiscovery work); only specific private data is encrypted to its owner: reminders, agent memory, observer frames, push leases, preference blobs and key backups.
how: VISION.md states one model of TLS in transit and storage-layer encryption at rest, with NIP-44 end-to-end DMs a future consideration; NIP-44 is used for kinds 30300 (reminders), 30174 (engrams), 24200 (observer), 44200 (metrics), push leases and nip44_encrypt_to_self blobs; NIP-17 gift wraps are accepted but excluded from search.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Space content must stay server-readable for retrieval and policy; the pattern of encrypting only owner-private records (reminders, memory) fits the personal agent boundary.

name: Pod-to-pod QUIC mesh with Redis-fenced ownership for sessions and audio
what: Relay replicas form an authenticated mesh so a user connected to one pod can be served by state owned by another, including live huddle audio, without a central media server.
how: buzz-relay-mesh runs one iroh endpoint per runtime with attested boot-unique identity, scuttlebutt membership gossip with phi-accrual failure detection, and a fenced wire contract carrying reliable streams and realtime datagrams; the stated law is that mesh membership is a hint and the Redis fenced generation is the arbiter; BUZZ_MESH=off yields exact single-instance behavior.
verevonRelevance: Not needed for a request-response BFF, but the principle that gossip is advisory while a fenced external store arbitrates ownership is a clean rule for any multi-instance session or sandbox lease.
notes: Medium confidence: read the crate overview and module boundaries, not the protocol internals.

name: Resume and repair after disconnect: live subscription first, then bounded backfill
what: After a drop the client reconnects, re-subscribes before backfilling so no event falls into the gap, and repairs a channel from the last seen time in bounded pages.
how: ARCHITECTURE.md states the consumption invariant (open the live subscription before or overlapping the finite history REQ) and a rule that a terminal CLOSED must release client-side subscription ownership in the same step; channel_reconnect_repair builds a since-based repair filter over fifteen structural kinds capped at 500 per page with an until plus before_id cursor; unread_catch_up.rs restores observed unread natively.
verevonRelevance: The subscribe-before-backfill rule and releasing ownership on terminal close are exactly the bugs a new Spaces SSE or WebSocket client will hit.
notes: Two incident-derived rules are recorded as PR numbers in the doc, a sign they were learned the hard way.

name: Postgres 17 partitioned event store with documented (unmeasured) scale targets
what: One monthly-partitioned events table holds all content with a generated search column; the stated target is 10,000 humans, 50,000 agents and about 600,000 events a day.
how: schema/partitions and a partition manager with audit and serving-safe gauges; community_id leads every key; Prometheus and OTLP telemetry with leader-only fleet gauges and a replica-only telemetry reader; the scale table in VISION.md is a target, not a measurement.
verevonRelevance: Gives a sizing reference (about 7 events per second average) for how small a chat-plus-agents workload actually is relative to what Verevon already stores.
notes: The one measured scale study in the repo is the Redis bus harness; no end-to-end load test result is published.

name: Self-hosting kit: compose stack, Helm chart and a single multi-call agent binary
what: An operator can run a community with one compose file (relay, Postgres, Redis, object storage, optional Caddy) or a Helm chart, and agents ship as one small binary that behaves as the harness, the agent or the git helpers depending on its name.
how: deploy/compose holds compose.yml, a dev variant, a Caddy overlay and run.sh for admin tasks; deploy/charts/buzz has a values schema, CI values and optional operator CronJobs; the sprig crate dispatches on argv0 to buzz-acp, buzz-agent, git-credential-nostr or git-sign-nostr so one musl-static binary suffices inside a Pod or container; Hermit pins the toolchain.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is hosted, but the argv0 multi-call binary is a neat way to ship one agent-side executable for a sandbox image, and the compose-first onboarding lowers evaluation friction.

name: Moderation as a closed loop: private reports, queue, signed actions, tombstones, notices
what: Any member can report a message in a few clicks; owners and admins see a private queue grouped by target and act in one step (dismiss, delete, kick, timeout, ban or escalate); the room sees a removal tombstone, the restricted person is told why and for how long, and the reporter hears the outcome.
how: NIP-56 kind 1984 reports land in a moderation_reports table (reporter identity never shown to the reported author; status open, processing, resolved, dismissed, escalated); actions are signed commands recorded in moderation_actions with separate private and public reasons; authority comes from the tenant roster through one authorize_moderation_action seam (community owner or admin community-wide, channel owner or admin per channel, no moderator tier); a timeout disables the composer with a visible countdown; notices arrive as DMs from the relay identity, which the client recognizes and locks against replies.
verevonRelevance: Spaces mixing humans and agents will need report, review and restrict flows; the report-is-a-signal-not-a-trigger rule and the honest tombstone are copyable, and an agent should be reportable like a person.
notes: Slack and Teams offer richer admin tooling (DLP, auto-actions); Buzz's strength is the clean human-in-the-loop design. No automod, and escalation is a hook with no consumer inbox.

name: Enforcement at the identity seam, cascading from owner to agents
what: A ban takes effect at authentication, disconnects the banned key everywhere, and also blocks every agent that key owns; a timeout blocks writes with a stated expiry.
how: Auth consults a community-ban verdict that fails closed on a database error; a ban on the principal blocks it and a ban on its NIP-OA owner blocks the agent; matched_principal (self or owner) is audit-only so the client never learns which; timeout state is enforced on write paths and surfaced to the composer.
verevonRelevance: When a Space member is removed, their personal agents must lose access in the same step; Buzz's owner-cascade is the rule, and Verevon already propagates membership revocation, so confirm agents are included.

name: Per-community hash-chain audit log (keyless; chain verification not wired)
what: Every accepted event, channel change, membership change, auth success or failure, rate-limit hit and media upload is appended to a per-community chain so edits to a single row are detectable.
how: audit_log rows are keyed by (community_id, seq) with SHA-256 over a tagged TLV encoding (version 2) that folds in the community id, sequence, timestamp, action, actor, object, canonical JSON detail and previous hash; writes serialize on a per-community advisory lock; BUZZ_AUDIT_ENABLED defaults on; the SECURITY.md text states the chain is tamper-evident but not tamper-resistant because it is keyless. AuditService::verify_chain is exercised only by tests: no relay path, CLI command or job calls it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon audit-core logs tool actions but has no Space-scoped chain; if tamper-evidence is wanted, also schedule verification and anchor heads externally, which Buzz does not.
notes: Medium confidence on the not-wired claim (grep of non-test callers across crates, including buzz-admin). SECURITY.md also calls it designed for SOX and eDiscovery use, but no export tooling exists. Audited actions exclude agent tool calls and moderation reads.

name: Formally modeled multi-tenant isolation with conformance replay
what: The claim that one community can never see another's events, profiles, DMs, search hits, audit chain or error strings is backed by models and a checker, not only tests.
how: A TLA+ model (MultiTenantRelay.tla) and a Tamarin model (MultiTenantAuth.spthy) with mutation testing; buzz-conformance replays relay traces against the model; docs/multi-tenant-conformance.md is a surface-by-surface table (host binding, tokens, membership, profiles, events, channels, workflows, search, Redis, media, git, agents, audit) with migration gates such as every tenant table carrying community_id and RLS; the host is the sole tenant selector and unknown hosts fail closed.
verevonRelevance: Verevon org isolation relies on JWT-derived org ids and Control decisions; a surface-by-surface conformance table plus trace replay would harden the Space aggregate, which spans four planes.
notes: Best-in-class among the peers reviewed for evidence of isolation; Slack and Teams publish no comparable artifacts.

name: Durable whole-community deletion with owner approval, checkpoints and an operator job
what: An owner can request deletion of an entire community; a digest-bound inventory is frozen and approved, and a resumable operator job deletes data across Postgres, Redis and object storage with checkpoints.
how: buzz-deletion engine with requests, approvals, checkpoints, executor heartbeats and manifest-key tables; buzz-admin deletions submit, approve, abort, unblock, run and drain; a Kubernetes CronJob (disabled by default) forbids overlap and retries because the store, not the scheduler, is authoritative; the pod receives only connection values, not the relay key or hook secrets; operator-origin requests never auto-progress.
verevonRelevance: Maps to the Verevon Space deletion saga and per-plane receipts; Buzz's choice that the durable store owns retry state, with Kubernetes retries off, is the same at-least-once discipline.
notes: Covers whole-community deletion only; there is no per-user erase or per-message retention policy.

name: Federated enterprise identity: stateless NIP-FI assertions (client flow still planned)
what: A relay can require that a key be bound to a company identity: a signed assertion from the identity provider adapter plus proof of the key, verified offline, with the issuer able to disconnect sessions.
how: The relay verifies a compact JWS against per-issuer JWKS snapshots, requires the (issuer, subject) tuple, community audience and fresh NIP-42 proof of possession; modes shadow, enforce and deny-protected; JWKS fetches are SSRF-guarded; an authenticated issuer-to-relay disconnect API supports revocation; the Desktop side only gates by build-time relay allowlist and the browser login, assertion fetch and session checks are marked planned in the guide. No SAML, SCIM or user provisioning exists.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has better-auth SSO; the useful idea is binding a per-agent or per-device key to an SSO identity with an offline-verifiable assertion and an issuer-driven disconnect.
notes: Medium confidence on production readiness: relay code is extensive, the client flow is documented as planned.

name: Information-flow control for agents (draft design plus an unused label crate)
what: A proposal to stop an agent from leaking what it learned in a private room into a wider one: a trusted broker holds the agent's key, each running copy is bound to one audience, and the broker refuses to publish to a broader audience unless a human approves the exact content and destination.
how: The design doc defines audience-bound agent instances, keyless agent processes calling a closed set of semantic operations, audience-labeled managed memory with membership epochs, and declassification by short-lived human approval; ifc-core implements reader-set confidentiality labels and an egress check; ifc-core is a workspace member that no other crate depends on, and the doc is marked Draft, dated 27 August 2026.
verevonRelevance: This is the closest thing to Verevon's rule that Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL; the audience-bound instance and the broker that checks egress against reader sets are worth adopting for personal agents invited into shared rooms.
notes: Design only; the doc admits it does not stop exfiltration through files, network or tools.

name: Outbound egress guard that refuses key-backup material at thirteen boundaries
what: The desktop refuses to send an encrypted key backup to any relay or admin API, even by accident, and a build test fails if a new send path skips the check.
how: egress_guard.rs scans text for ncryptsec1 in lower and upper case, is wired into relay submit funnels, profile sync, the native WebSocket send loop, huddle STT, engram submission and admin requests, and an inventory-completeness test asserts every events URL construction site calls it; raw nsec transit through the encrypted pairing session is deliberately out of scope and called separate DLP work.
verevonRelevance: A tiny, testable outbound content guard with a coverage test is a model for keeping secrets out of agent-authored room messages in Verevon.
notes: Pattern-based and key-material only; not general DLP.

name: Per-principal rate limits and replay guards at admission
what: Humans and agents get separate message and request quotas, enforced across relay nodes, and a signed HTTP request cannot be replayed.
how: A Redis fixed-window limiter (its own comment admits a token bucket would be smoother) with tiers for human messages (60 a minute), human WebSocket events (10 a second with a 5-second burst window), agent standard (120), elevated (300) and platform (600) messages; fail closed with a rate-limit message addressed to the rejected frame; Redis-backed NIP-98 and NIP-FI command replay guards with shared seen-sets; ARCHITECTURE.md still says no limiter is enforced, which is stale.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs an agent-aware message quota per Space and member so one chatty agent cannot flood a room; Buzz's agent tiers by token class are a starting point.
notes: The doc-versus-code conflict shows ARCHITECTURE.md lags the code.

name: Enumerated-deny SSRF guard with IP pinning, used by webhooks, link previews and JWKS
what: Server-side and client-side fetches of user-supplied URLs refuse private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade, documentation, multicast and embedded-IPv4 addresses, and pin the resolved IP so DNS rebinding cannot swap it.
how: buzz_core::network::is_not_global_unicast and is_private_ip classify addresses (including IPv4 embedded in mapped, NAT64 and SIIT forms); workflow call_webhook resolves, checks, then connects to the checked IP with redirects disabled and a 1 MiB cap; desktop link preview and the NIP-FI JWKS fetcher call the same helpers.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon feature that fetches a URL on a user's or agent's behalf (link preview, webhook, connector) should reuse one such guard; Quarry already owns crawl policy, so use it as the reference check.
notes: Enumerated deny means unlisted special-use ranges pass (the doc says so).

name: Media reads are authenticated and tenant-scoped but not channel-ACL gated
what: Uploaded images and files cannot be fetched anonymously, but anyone who is a member of the community and knows the content hash can fetch a blob even from a private channel.
how: GET and HEAD on /media/{sha256.ext} require a Blossom get auth event scoped to the host or blob hash and bind the read to the header-resolved tenant; the conformance table records as a deferred gap that reads are not gated by the ACL of the message the blob was attached to.
verevonRelevance: A direct lesson for Space attachments: bind blob reads to the room ACL (or an owner-plane grant), not just to the tenant, or private-room files leak to anyone with a hash.
notes: Content-addressed storage makes this a structural risk.

name: Retention is mostly absent: ephemeral channels, local observer retention and push tombstones only
what: The relay never expires ordinary messages; the only expiry features are ephemeral channels that archive after idle time, a 30-day default for locally archived observer frames on the owner's machine, and retained push-revocation tombstones.
how: channels.ttl_seconds refreshes on each event insert via a deferred trigger; archive retention is one global observer_retention_days setting (default 30, max 36,500) while metrics are kept indefinitely; schema comments state the relay does not expire events; no org-level retention schedule, legal hold or per-room policy was found.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's ZDR propagation and deletion receipts are ahead here; if Spaces keep human chat, add a per-room retention and legal-hold model rather than relying on whole-space deletion.
notes: Medium confidence: absence from grep of schema and handlers.

name: Mobile age gate and terms acceptance on join
what: On join the user must accept the community's terms and privacy policy, and the mobile app can ask the OS for an age signal and show a restriction page for under-18 users.
how: Join-policy acceptances are stored per community and checked at claim time; the mobile age_gate feature asks the OS for an age signal at launch (30-second bound, access never waits on it) and blocks only on an explicit valid upper bound under 18; the relay config also has an optional BUZZ_AGE_ATTESTATION_REQUIRED switch.
verevonRelevance: Consumer-product detail; relevant only if Verevon Spaces admit consumers or minors.

name: [Not built] SSO provisioning, SCIM, DLP, eDiscovery export, data residency and legal hold
what: Beyond the federated-identity assertion path there is no SAML or SCIM, no content DLP or sensitivity labels, no compliance export or hold, and no per-tenant data-residency control.
how: Grep found OIDC only inside the agent's LLM OAuth; the audit log has no export path and verify is unwired; local archive export is a user-side save, not a compliance tool; multi-community hosting is one shared Postgres and Redis per deployment.
verevonRelevance: Teams sets the enterprise bar here (Purview, eDiscovery, residency); neither Buzz nor Verevon Spaces meets it yet.
notes: Absence claims are grep-level and medium confidence.

name: Tauri 2 desktop shell with Rust-owned state and a large IPC surface
what: A native desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) with single-instance behavior, remembered window state, an overlay title bar, a tray menu that shows running agents, and macOS extras (application menu, window vibrancy, mouse back and forward buttons).
how: Tauri 2 plugins for deep-link, single-instance, window-state, dialog, updater, process, global-shortcut and notification; the React frontend talks to Rust through about 380 #[tauri::command] functions registered in lib.rs, so keys, relay sessions, the local archive and agent processes live in Rust and never in the webview; a minimum 900 by 650 window with an overlay title bar.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is browser-first so none of this ports directly; the principle of keeping credentials and long-lived connections in the trusted native layer matches the BFF rule that browsers hold no upstream credentials.
notes: Slack and Teams desktop apps are Electron shells around a web client; Buzz is the opposite, with logic in Rust.

name: buzz:// deep links with a cold-start pending queue
what: Links open a message, channel, thread, join invite, add-community prompt or identity-binding flow, even when the app was not running; links pasted into chat render as chips.
how: Scheme registered through tauri-plugin-deep-link; handle_deep_link_url parses join, add-community, channel, message, entity and nostr-bind forms with allowlists; links received before the webview is ready are queued in three pending queues (community, navigation, entity) that the frontend drains on start; single-instance forwards a second launch's URL.
verevonRelevance: A Space needs stable links to rooms, messages and runs that survive login redirects; the explicit pending queue is the pattern for a link that arrives before the client is ready.

name: Auto-update with independent desktop, relay and mobile release lanes
what: The desktop app updates itself (AppImage only on Linux), with a visible update card in the sidebar; releases go through immutable candidate pull requests, signed macOS builds and a separate mobile release-candidate lane.
how: tauri-plugin-updater with endpoint and public key injected at build time (endpoints empty in tauri.conf.json); is_auto_update_supported returns false for non-AppImage Linux installs; SidebarUpdateCard and UpdateChecker; RELEASING.md describes three independent lanes (desktop, relay image, mobile candidate tags) and a merge-is-authorization rule for release PRs; the Windows build ships unsigned.
verevonRelevance: Not applicable to a web app, but the immutable-candidate release model with human merge as authorization is worth considering for Verevon's gated plane releases.
notes: Windows unsigned installer and Git Bash prerequisite (README.md:184) are rough edges.

name: Keyboard-first navigation without a command palette
what: Cmd/Ctrl+K searches everything; Cmd/Ctrl+F searches the current channel; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K starts a new message, +N creates a channel, +O browses channels and +A goes Home; Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles a huddle; a mark-as-read shortcut exists; there is no general command palette.
how: useAppShellKeyboardShortcuts registers the shortcuts (the huddle shortcut in capture phase so composer focus cannot swallow it); useMarkAsReadShortcuts, zoom, reload and settings shortcut hooks; a KeyboardShortcutsCard lists them; push-to-talk is a native global shortcut.
verevonRelevance: A Verevon Space command palette (jump to room, run an action, address an agent) is a natural use of the existing action registry; Buzz leaves it unbuilt, so Slack and Teams are the reference.
notes: Slack and Teams both have richer command surfaces.

name: Mobile client: Flutter, three-tab shell, biometrics, offline-first intent
what: iOS and Android apps with a floating tab bar (Home with channels and DMs, Activity inbox, Search), community switcher, huddles, voice notes, camera capture, QR pairing, biometric lock, app badge and deep links.
how: Flutter with hooks_riverpod; mobile/lib/features covers activity, channels, forum, home, invites, pairing, profile, pulse, search and settings; local_auth biometrics, mobile_scanner pairing, record and just_audio voice, app_badge_plus, share_plus; an APNs NotificationService extension for content-free push; the spec doc VISION_MOBILE.md takes priority over code and says not everything is implemented.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no mobile client; the three-tab shell (conversations, activity, search) and a QR plus short-code pairing are a minimal viable shape for a companion app.
notes: Android push is not implemented (APNs only).

name: Web client is a repository browser and invite landing page, not a chat client
what: Opening a community URL in a browser shows its repositories, file tree, README, commits and a Connect on Buzz button, plus an invite page for join codes; there is no way to read or post messages from a browser.
how: web/ is a Vite React app with routes for index, invite/$code and repos (list, detail, blob); isomorphic-git with lightning-fs clones in the browser; NIP-98 signing in the browser for invite claim; the chat experience exists only in the Tauri desktop and Flutter mobile apps.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is browser-native, which is a real advantage over Buzz for adoption in companies that cannot install apps; do not copy the app-only chat model.
notes: The README advertises web access to repos only; Slack and Teams both have full web clients.

name: Theme engine that derives the whole UI from a code-editor theme
what: Users pick from a large catalog of editor themes (light and dark pairs, with a Buzz default), and the whole interface palette is derived from the theme's key colors; a community can carry its own theme.
how: theme-loader reads Shiki theme JSON and extracts background, foreground, comment and git colors; adaptive-theme.ts derives shadcn CSS variables and detects light or dark from luminance; THEME_PAIRS group light and dark variants; CommunityThemeController applies a per-community theme from a kind 30078 event; an animated Grainient background is optional; build-time BUZZ_THEME_NAME variables brand a build.
verevonRelevance: Per-org or per-Space theming is a cheap brand and identity cue in a multi-org product; deriving a palette from a handful of colors keeps contrast logic in one place.

name: Accessibility posture: ARIA coverage, reduced-motion gating and screen-reader text in tests
what: The app targets WCAG 2.1 AA, gates animation on the reduced-motion preference in dozens of components, and its end-to-end tests assert accessible names and screen-reader status text for tricky states.
how: aria- attributes appear in about 400 desktop TSX files and reduced-motion checks in about 70 files (grep counts); canvas save focus management moves focus to the surviving control after the editor unmounts; availability tests check visible badges plus accessible names; VISION_MOBILE.md requires screen readers, text scaling and reduced motion; no automated axe audit was found.
verevonRelevance: Specify focus return and accessible-status text for every Space dialog and status chip in the requirement, as Buzz does in its regression gates.
notes: Counts come from my own grep during this pass and exclude Dart; quality is unmeasured.

name: [Not built] Localization, multi-language UI and RTL
what: The desktop, web and admin clients have no translation layer; UI strings are English literals.
how: No i18n library or message catalogs in desktop, web or admin-web dependencies; the mobile pubspec lists intl only for formatting; no ARB bundles.
verevonRelevance: Slack and Teams ship dozens of languages; Verevon serves Nordic customers, so plan a message-catalog layer early rather than retrofitting.
notes: Absence established by dependency inspection and grep (medium confidence).

name: Platform edges: Windows needs Git Bash, unsigned installer, Linux media shim
what: Agents run commands under bash, so Windows users must install Git for Windows; the Windows installer is unsigned and Linux webviews need extra media and rendering workarounds.
how: managed_agents/git_bash.rs discovers Git Bash and a prerequisite check surfaces in onboarding; BUZZ_SHELL overrides; linux_media.rs bridges WebKitGTK getUserMedia; docs/linux-rendering-troubleshooting.md; README flags SmartScreen on the unsigned build.
verevonRelevance: Reinforces hosting agents server-side: Buzz's local-process model forces per-OS prerequisites onto every user.

name: Navigation model: community rail, pinned feature menu, grouped conversations, right-side panel
what: A narrow rail switches communities; the sidebar leads with a search box and a fixed menu (Home inbox, Agents, Workflows, Pulse, Projects), then groups conversations as Starred, Channels, Forums, Direct messages and custom sections; the channel view opens threads, canvas, members or an agent session in a resizable right panel.
how: File-based routes for home, agents, pulse, reminders, settings, workflows, projects, new message, channel and forum post; AppSidebarPinnedHeader holds the search and feature entries; four fixed channel groups plus user sections; RightAuxiliaryPane and the shared auxiliary-panel shell give threads, canvas, members and agent sessions one resizable, remembered-width container.
verevonRelevance: A Space sidebar should group conversations by kind, keep agents and the inbox as first-class destinations, and use one side panel for threads, runs and artifacts rather than separate pages.
notes: Slack's information architecture with agents and projects added; discoverability of Workflows, Pulse and Projects is hurt by preview gating.

name: Sidebar organization that follows you: stars, custom sections, per-group sort, drag and drop
what: Users star channels, create their own sections, sort each group alphabetically or by recent activity, drag channels between sections, and see a More-unread button when unread conversations are off-screen; all of it syncs across devices.
how: Per-group sort keys (starred, channels, forums, dms, section:<id>) with alpha or recent modes; sections and stars stored as synced blobs; dnd-kit sorting through SidebarDnd; MoreUnreadButton with overflow counts above and below; hidden DMs resurface on new activity; per-relay local storage keys avoid bleeding across communities.
verevonRelevance: Verevon lacks any per-user room organization; custom sections plus alpha or recent sort per group are the smallest set that Slack users expect.

name: Composer activity strip: who is typing and which agents are working, with live headlines
what: Above the composer, a row shows who is typing and which agents are working; with a single working agent it rotates short headlines of what it is doing, and clicking it opens that agent's live session panel.
how: ChannelComposerActivityAccessory merges TypingIndicatorRow and BotActivityComposerAction; the action reads the owner-side transcript for the single working agent, derives headlines (getActivityHeadline) rotating every 2.2 seconds with a shimmer, opens a hover popover listing working agents, and routes to onOpenAgentSession.
verevonRelevance: The cheapest, highest-value room cue for agent work: a one-line ambient status next to the composer that expands into the run, rather than streaming everything into the timeline.
notes: Headlines depend on owner-only transcript data, so non-owners see only a generic working state (INF from the transcript hook usage).

name: Empty states with action cards and an agent-led composer nudge
what: A new channel intro shows contextual action cards (add people, add an agent, add files, browse or create channels); the Welcome channel offers browse, create and create-an-agent cards and a composer banner that animates a suggested first agent.
how: useChannelIntro assembles an intro block per channel kind (welcome, project home, ordinary, DM) with action callbacks; WelcomeComposerBanner has prompt, complete, dismissing and hidden states with reduced-motion handling; ChannelIntroBlock and DirectMessageIntroAvatarStack render intros; a plain Select a channel state covers no selection.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's empty Space needs the same first-run guidance (invite, add an agent, attach knowledge); offering the action cards in the timeline's empty state keeps the next step where the user is looking.

name: Message row anatomy for mixed human and agent rooms
what: Messages show author, agent badge and owner (managed by), a distinct bot avatar, an address prefix when a message is aimed at an agent, an unread divider, day dividers, system rows, diffs, voice notes, link previews and setup cards.
how: MessageRow composes MessageAuthorWithIndicators (role, owner pubkey), BotIdenticon, MessageAgentOwner, MessageAgentAddressPrefix, UnreadDivider, DayDivider, SystemMessageRow, DiffMessage, link-preview and config-nudge attachments; the owner label reads managed by on mobile and desktop; moderation tombstones and membership notices have their own row types.
verevonRelevance: A Verevon room post is currently one model turn; typed row kinds (human, agent, system, run, approval) with owner labels give the timeline the vocabulary it needs.

name: Timeline scroll anchoring and jump-to-latest across desktop and mobile
what: The timeline keeps your place while history loads or new messages arrive, pins to the bottom only when you are there, and offers a jump-to-latest control; the mobile client also tracks IME height and initial thread tail settling.
how: useAnchoredScroll with an anchoredScrollPolicy module and lifecycle, observer-feed and mount-pin tests; virtualized lists (TanStack Virtual, virtua patched); mobile jump_to_latest_button, laid_out_viewport, ime_metrics_settle_observer and initial_thread_tail_settle in the channel feature.
verevonRelevance: Room timelines that grow with agent output need scroll anchoring rules written down and tested; Buzz has invested in this (a patched virtual list) and so should Verevon before enabling live streaming.

name: Honest-state UX: unknown is not zero, unverified is not failed, and nothing goes silent
what: Across features the UI distinguishes states instead of collapsing them: an unreadable count shows nothing rather than zero, a failed presence read is unknown rather than offline, a saved-but-unverified canvas shows a notice rather than an error, and running tool rows mutate in place.
how: Stated rules in VISION_ACTIVITY (never go dark, honesty over guessing), docs/buzz-v1-read-state.md (absence means unavailable, show no count rather than zero), docs/agent-availability.md (unknown is not Offline), the canvas unverified-save notice with focus return, MessageTimelineErrorCard and per-section failed notices in project work items.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's unavailable[] contract already points this way; make it a UI rule (every chip, count and status has an explicit unknown state) and test it with held-pending reads as Buzz does.
notes: The most consistent design discipline found in the repo; it shows in docs, code and tests.

name: Motion and delight with reduced-motion gating (emoji bursts, poof delete, animated counts)
what: Emoji reactions can burst on screen, deleted items poof away with a sound, counts animate, and loading text shimmers; the same components check the reduced-motion preference and a conversation-density setting (compact, comfortable, spacious) adjusts spacing.
how: EmojiBurstProvider and PoofBurstProvider (five-frame sprite, 430 ms) are global providers; Shimmer and AnimatedCount are shared components; motion/react with useReducedMotion in about 70 files; conversationDensityPreference stores a device-level density in localStorage with a safe fallback.
verevonRelevance: Culture and delight features are explicitly ship blockers in VISION.md; for a company product they are optional, but density and reduced-motion handling should be in the first design system pass.

name: Selection-to-context workflow: select items in a list, then discuss them with an agent or a channel
what: In Projects you can multi-select work items, commits or reviews and send them as context to an agent chat or open a discussion channel about them; the selection count is visible and the context strip names what is attached.
how: ProjectSelectableGroup, ProjectsSelectionCountMenu, ProjectSelectionDiscussAction and useProjectDiscussInChannel feed buildProjectsViewAgentContext, which produces the quoted context block with caps; the agent chat panel shows ProjectAgentContextStrip and submitted-context pills.
verevonRelevance: A strong human-to-agent hand-off interaction for Verevon Spaces: select the items you mean, then ask; the user sees exactly which objects the agent receives.
notes: Tied to Projects objects; not yet general to chat messages.
